15.s:
athaitadupayogāya yāgastāvannirūpyate /
tatra dīkṣaiva bhoge ca muktau cāyātyupāyatām // 1
15.d:
अथैतदुपयोगाय यागस्तावन्निरूप्यते ।
तत्र दीक्षैव भोगे च मुक्तौ चायात्युपायताम् ॥ 1
15.m: Now, for the purpose of this, sacrificial worship is first described; / in that context, initiation alone comes to serve as the means both to enjoyment and to liberation.

15.s:
svayaṃ saṃskārayogādvā tadaṅgaṃ tatpradarśyate /
yo yatrābhilaṣedbhogān sa tatraiva niyojitaḥ // 2
15.d:
स्वयं संस्कारयोगाद्वा तदङ्गं तत्प्रदर्श्यते ।
यो यत्राभिलषेद्भोगान् स तत्रैव नियोजितः ॥ 2
15.m: Either spontaneously or through purification, that subordinate element is shown: / wherever one desires enjoyments, there he is conjoined,

15.s:
siddhibhāṅmantraśaktyeti śrīmatsvāyaṃbhuve vibhuḥ /
yogyatāvaśato yatra vāsanā yasya tatra saḥ // 3
15.d:
सिद्धिभाङ्मन्त्रशक्त्येति श्रीमत्स्वायंभुवे विभुः ।
योग्यतावशतो यत्र वासना यस्य तत्र सः ॥ 3
15.m: sharing in spiritual accomplishment through the power of mantras—thus the all-pervading Lord in the venerable Svāyambhuva. / Under the influence of capacity, where one's latent impression lies, there he

15.s:
yojyo na cyavate tasmāditi śrīmālinīmate /
vadanbhogādyupāyatvaṃ dīkṣāyāḥ prāha no guruḥ // 4
15.d:
योज्यो न च्यवते तस्मादिति श्रीमालिनीमते ।
वदन्भोगाद्युपायत्वं दीक्षायाः प्राह नो गुरुः ॥ 4
15.m: is to be conjoined; he does not fall from that—thus in the venerable doctrine of the Mālinī. / Stating that initiation is the means to enjoyment and the like, our guru said:

15.s:
na cādhikāritā dīkṣāṃ vinā yoge'sti śāṅkare /
na ca yogādhikāritvamekamevānayā bhavet // 5
15.d:
न चाधिकारिता दीक्षां विना योगेऽस्ति शाङ्करे ।
न च योगाधिकारित्वमेकमेवानया भवेत् ॥ 5
15.m: "There is no competence in Śaiva yoga without initiation, / nor does competence in yoga alone come to be by means of it;

15.s:
api mantrādhikāritvaṃ muktiśca śivadīkṣayā /
ityasminmālinīvākye sākṣānmokṣābhyupāyatā // 6
15.d:
अपि मन्त्राधिकारित्वं मुक्तिश्च शिवदीक्षया ।
इत्यस्मिन्मालिनीवाक्ये साक्षान्मोक्षाभ्युपायता ॥ 6
15.m: there is also competence in mantras, and liberation through initiation into Śiva." / In this statement of the Mālinī, initiation as a direct means to liberation

15.s:
dīkṣāyāḥ kathitā prācyagranthena punarucyate /
pāramparyeṇa saṃskṛtyā mokṣabhogābhyupāyatā // 7
15.d:
दीक्षायाः कथिता प्राच्यग्रन्थेन पुनरुच्यते ।
पारम्पर्येण संस्कृत्या मोक्षभोगाभ्युपायता ॥ 7
15.m: is stated. By the earlier text, however, it is again spoken of / as an indirect means to liberation and enjoyment through purification.

15.s:
yeṣāmadhyavasāyo'sti na vidyāṃ pratyaśaktitaḥ /
sukhopāyamidaṃ teṣāṃ vidhānamuditaṃ guroḥ // 8
15.d:
येषामध्यवसायोऽस्ति न विद्यां प्रत्यशक्तितः ।
सुखोपायमिदं तेषां विधानमुदितं गुरोः ॥ 8
15.m: "For those who have no determination regarding gnosis because of inability, / this easy means, the rite of the guru, has been spoken of."

15.s:
iti śrīmanmataṅgākhye hyuktā mokṣābhyupāyatā /
samyagjñānasvabhāvā hi vidyā sākṣādvimocikā // 9
15.d:
इति श्रीमन्मतङ्गाख्ये ह्युक्ता मोक्षाभ्युपायता ।
सम्यग्ज्ञानस्वभावा हि विद्या साक्षाद्विमोचिका ॥ 9
15.m: Thus indeed in the work called the venerable Mataṅga it is declared that [initiation] is a means to liberation; / for gnosis, whose nature is correct knowledge, directly liberates.

15.s:
uktaṃ tatraiva tattvānāṃ kāryakāraṇabhāvataḥ /
heyādeyatvakathane vidyāpāda iti sphuṭam // 10
15.d:
उक्तं तत्रैव तत्त्वानां कार्यकारणभावतः ।
हेयादेयत्वकथने विद्यापाद इति स्फुटम् ॥ 10
15.m: It is stated in that very work, in the Vidyāpāda, clearly / in the explanation of what is to be abandoned and adopted according to the causal relation among the principles of reality:

15.s:
tatrāśaktāstu ye teṣāṃ dīkṣācaryāsamādhayaḥ /
te vidyāpūrvakā yasmāttasmājjñānyuttamottamaḥ // 11
15.d:
तत्राशक्तास्तु ये तेषां दीक्षाचर्यासमाधयः ।
ते विद्यापूर्वका यस्मात्तस्माज्ज्ञान्युत्तमोत्तमः ॥ 11
15.m: "Those, however, who are incapable in that regard—their initiation, conduct, and meditations / are preceded by gnosis; therefore, the knower is the highest of the high."

15.s:
jñānaṃ ca śāstrāttaccāpi śrāvyo nādīkṣito yataḥ /
ato'sya saṃskriyāmātropayogo dīkṣayā kṛtaḥ // 12
15.d:
ज्ञानं च शास्त्रात्तच्चापि श्राव्यो नादीक्षितो यतः ।
अतोऽस्य संस्क्रियामात्रोपयोगो दीक्षया कृतः ॥ 12
15.m: And gnosis comes from the scripture, and an uninitiated person should not be made to hear that; / therefore, through initiation only his purification is effected.

15.s:
yatra tatrāstu guruṇā yojito'sau phalaṃ punaḥ /
svavijñānocitaṃ yāti jñānītyuktaṃ purā kila // 13
15.d:
यत्र तत्रास्तु गुरुणा योजितोऽसौ फलं पुनः ।
स्वविज्ञानोचितं याति ज्ञानीत्युक्तं पुरा किल ॥ 13
15.m: Wherever he may be conjoined by the guru, the knower, however, / attains the fruit suitable to his own insight; thus indeed it was said before.

15.s:
yasya tvīśaprasādena divyā kācana yogyatā /
guroḥ śiśośca tau naiva prati dīkṣopayogitā // 14
15.d:
यस्य त्वीशप्रसादेन दिव्या काचन योग्यता ।
गुरोः शिशोश्च तौ नैव प्रति दीक्षोपयोगिता ॥ 14
15.m: For one, however, who has some divine capacity through the grace of the Lord, / between guru and disciple there is no need of initiation for those two.

15.s:
jñānameva tadā dīkṣā śrītraiśikanirūpaṇāt /
sarvaśāstrārthavettṛtvamakasmāccāsya jāyate // 15
15.d:
ज्ञानमेव तदा दीक्षा श्रीत्रैशिकनिरूपणात् ।
सर्वशास्त्रार्थवेत्तृत्वमकस्माच्चास्य जायते ॥ 15
15.m: Then gnosis itself is initiation, according to the determination of the venerable Trika; / and unexpectedly there arises for him the understanding of the meaning of all scriptures.

15.s:
iti śrīmālinīnītyā yaḥ sāṃsiddhikasaṃvidaḥ /
sa uttamādhikārī syājjñānavānhi gururmataḥ // 16
15.d:
इति श्रीमालिनीनीत्या यः सांसिद्धिकसंविदः ।
स उत्तमाधिकारी स्याज्ज्ञानवान्हि गुरुर्मतः ॥ 16
15.m: Thus, according to the principle of the venerable Mālinī, he whose consciousness is innate / would be an aspirant of the highest qualification, for the knower is considered a guru.

15.s:
ātmane vā parebhyo vā hitārthī cetayedidam /
ityuktyā mālinīśāstre tatsarvaṃ prakaṭīkṛtam // 17
15.d:
आत्मने वा परेभ्यो वा हितार्थी चेतयेदिदम् ।
इत्युक्त्या मालिनीशास्त्रे तत्सर्वं प्रकटीकृतम् ॥ 17
15.m: "Desiring the good either for oneself or for others, one should make this known"; / through this statement in the Mālinīśāstra, all of that has been made clear.

15.s:
jñānayogyāstathā keciccaryāyogyāstathāpare /
dīkṣāyogyā yogayogyā iti śrīkairaṇe vidhau // 18
15.d:
ज्ञानयोग्यास्तथा केचिच्चर्यायोग्यास्तथापरे ।
दीक्षायोग्या योगयोग्या इति श्रीकैरणे विधौ ॥ 18
15.m: Some are fit for gnosis, while others are fit for conduct; / some are fit for initiation, and some are fit for yoga: thus in the venerable Kiraṇa ritual.

15.s:
tatroktalakṣaṇaḥ karmayogajñānaviśāradaḥ /
uttarottaratābhūmyutkṛṣṭo gururudīritaḥ // 19
15.d:
तत्रोक्तलक्षणः कर्मयोगज्ञानविशारदः ।
उत्तरोत्तरताभूम्युत्कृष्टो गुरुरुदीरितः ॥ 19
15.m: There, the guru described with the stated characteristics, proficient in ritual, yoga, and gnosis, / is superior by reason of successively higher stages.

15.s:
sa ca prāguktaśaktyanyatamapātapavitritam /
parīkṣya pṛṣṭvā vā śiṣyaṃ dīkṣākarma samācaret // 20
15.d:
स च प्रागुक्तशक्त्यन्यतमपातपवित्रितम् ।
परीक्ष्य पृष्ट्वा वा शिष्यं दीक्षाकर्म समाचरेत् ॥ 20
15.m: And he, having examined or questioned the disciple purified by any one of the aforementioned descents of power, / should perform the rite of initiation.

15.s:
uktaṃ svacchandaśāstre ca śiṣyaṃ pṛcchedguruḥ svayam /
phalaṃ prārthayase yādṛktādṛksādhanamārabhe // 21
15.d:
उक्तं स्वच्छन्दशास्त्रे च शिष्यं पृच्छेद्गुरुः स्वयम् ।
फलं प्रार्थयसे यादृक्तादृक्साधनमारभे ॥ 21
15.m: And in the Svacchandaśāstra it is stated: "The guru himself should ask the disciple: / 'What kind of fruit do you pray for? I shall undertake that kind of means.'"

15.s:
vāsanābhedataḥ sādhyaprāptirmantrapracoditā /
mantramudrādhvadravyāṇāṃ home sādhāraṇā sthitiḥ // 22
15.d:
वासनाभेदतः साध्यप्राप्तिर्मन्त्रप्रचोदिता ।
मन्त्रमुद्राध्वद्रव्याणां होमे साधारणा स्थितिः ॥ 22
15.m: Attainment of the goal, impelled by the mantra, depends on the distinction of latent impressions; / the condition of mantras, seals, paths, and substances in the fire sacrifice is common [to all].

15.s:
vāsanābhedato bhinnaṃ śiṣyāṇāṃ ca guroḥ phalam /
sādhako dvividhaḥ śaivadharmā lokojjhitasthitiḥ // 23
15.d:
वासनाभेदतो भिन्नं शिष्याणां च गुरोः फलम् ।
साधको द्विविधः शैवधर्मा लोकोज्झितस्थितिः ॥ 23
15.m: The fruit for the disciples and for the guru is differentiated by the distinction of latent impressions. / The adept is twofold: one observing the Śaiva rule, whose state is devoid of worldly ways,

15.s:
lokadharmī phalākāṃkṣī śubhasthaścāśubhojjhitaḥ /
dvidhā mumukṣurnirbījaḥ samayādivivarjitaḥ // 24
15.d:
लोकधर्मी फलाकांक्षी शुभस्थश्चाशुभोज्झितः ।
द्विधा मुमुक्षुर्निर्बीजः समयादिविवर्जितः ॥ 24
15.m: and one observing worldly ways, desiring results, abiding in the auspicious and free from the inauspicious. / The seeker of liberation is twofold: seedless, devoid of rules and the like—

15.s:
bālabāliśavṛddhastrībhogabhugvyādhitādikaḥ /
anyaḥ sabījo yasyetthaṃ dīkṣoktā śivaśāsane // 25
15.d:
बालबालिशवृद्धस्त्रीभोगभुग्व्याधितादिकः ।
अन्यः सबीजो यस्येत्थं दीक्षोक्ता शिवशासने ॥ 25
15.m: a child, a simpleton, the aged, a woman, an enjoyer of pleasures, the sick, and so forth; / the other is with seed, for whom initiation is thus taught in the teaching of Śiva.

15.s:
vidvaddvandvasahānāṃ tu sabījā samayātmikā /
dīkṣānugrāhikā pālyā viśeṣasamayāstu taiḥ // 26
15.d:
विद्वद्द्वन्द्वसहानां तु सबीजा समयात्मिका ।
दीक्षानुग्राहिका पाल्या विशेषसमयास्तु तैः ॥ 26
15.m: For the wise and those enduring the pairs of opposites, [initiation is] with seed, consisting of rules; / the initiation confers grace, but the special rules must be observed by them.

15.s:
abhāvaṃ bhāvayetsamyakkarmaṇāṃ prācyabhāvinām /
mumukṣornirapekṣasya prārabdhrekaṃ na śādhayet // 27
15.d:
अभावं भावयेत्सम्यक्कर्मणां प्राच्यभाविनाम् ।
मुमुक्षोर्निरपेक्षस्य प्रारब्ध्रेकं न शाधयेत् ॥ 27
15.m: One should properly contemplate the non-existence of past and future karmas; / for a seeker of liberation who has no desires, one should not destroy the single operative karma.

15.s:
sādhakasya tu bhūtyarthamitthameva viśodhayet /
śivadharmiṇyasau dīkṣā lokadharmāpahāriṇī // 28
15.d:
साधकस्य तु भूत्यर्थमित्थमेव विशोधयेत् ।
शिवधर्मिण्यसौ दीक्षा लोकधर्मापहारिणी ॥ 28
15.m: For an adept, however, one should purify it in this very manner for the sake of prosperity. / This initiation for one observing the Śaiva rule removes worldly duty.

15.s:
adharmarūpiṇāmeva na śubhānāṃ tu śodhanam /
lokadharmiṇyasau dīkṣā mantrārādhanavarjitā // 29
15.d:
अधर्मरूपिणामेव न शुभानां तु शोधनम् ।
लोकधर्मिण्यसौ दीक्षा मन्त्राराधनवर्जिता ॥ 29
15.m: The purification is of those [karmas] consisting of demerit alone, not of auspicious ones; / this initiation is for one observing worldly duty, devoid of the worship of mantras.

15.s:
prārabdhadehabhede tu bhuṅkte'sāvaṇimādikam /
bhuktvordhvaṃ yāti yatraiṣa yukto'tha sakale'kale // 30
15.d:
प्रारब्धदेहभेदे तु भुङ्क्तेऽसावणिमादिकम् ।
भुक्त्वोर्ध्वं याति यत्रैष युक्तोऽथ सकलेऽकले ॥ 30
15.m: Upon the destruction of the operative body, he enjoys [powers] such as atomicity; / having enjoyed, he ascends above, where he is conjoined, whether in the embodied or the unembodied.

15.s:
samayācārapāśaṃ tu nirbījāyāṃ viśodhayet /
dīkṣāmātreṇa muktiḥ syādbhaktyā deve gurau sadā // 31
15.d:
समयाचारपाशं तु निर्बीजायां विशोधयेत् ।
दीक्षामात्रेण मुक्तिः स्याद्भक्त्या देवे गुरौ सदा ॥ 31
15.m: In the seedless [initiation], however, one should purify the bond of the conventional rule of conduct; / liberation occurs through initiation alone, through constant devotion to God and the guru.

15.s:
sadyonirvāṇadā seyaṃ nirbījā yeti bhaṇyate /
atītānāgatārabdhapāśatrayaviyojikā // 32
15.d:
सद्योनिर्वाणदा सेयं निर्बीजा येति भण्यते ।
अतीतानागतारब्धपाशत्रयवियोजिका ॥ 32
15.m: That which is called seedless brings immediate liberation, / severing the threefold bond of past, future, and commenced [karma].

15.s:
dīkṣāvasāne śuddhasya dehatyāge paraṃ padam /
dehatyāge sabījāyāṃ karmābhāvādvipadyate // 33
15.d:
दीक्षावसाने शुद्धस्य देहत्यागे परं पदम् ।
देहत्यागे सबीजायां कर्माभावाद्विपद्यते ॥ 33
15.m: Upon the cessation of initiation, the supreme state is attained by the purified soul at the abandonment of the body. / In the seeded [initiation], when the body is abandoned, he perishes [into liberation] due to the absence of karma.

15.s:
samayācārapāśaṃ tu dīkṣitaḥ pālayetsadā /
evaṃ pṛṣṭvā parijñāya vicārya ca guruḥ svayam // 34
15.d:
समयाचारपाशं तु दीक्षितः पालयेत्सदा ।
एवं पृष्ट्वा परिज्ञाय विचार्य च गुरुः स्वयम् ॥ 34
15.m: The initiate, however, must always observe the bond of the conventional rule of conduct. / Thus having asked, recognized, and reflected for himself, the guru

15.s:
ucitāṃ saṃvidhitsustāṃ vāsanāṃ tādṛśīṃ śrayet /
āyātaśaktipātasya dīkṣāṃ prati na daiśikaḥ // 35
15.d:
उचितां संविधित्सुस्तां वासनां तादृशीं श्रयेत् ।
आयातशक्तिपातस्य दीक्षां प्रति न दैशिकः ॥ 35
15.m: should adopt that suitable residual trace, wishing to construct it in such a manner. / The spiritual teacher should not show disregard towards the initiation

15.s:
avajñāṃ vidadhīteti śaṃbhunājñā nirūpitā /
svadhanena daridrasya kuryāddīkṣāṃ guruḥ svayam // 36
15.d:
अवज्ञां विदधीतेति शंभुनाज्ञा निरूपिता ।
स्वधनेन दरिद्रस्य कुर्याद्दीक्षां गुरुः स्वयम् ॥ 36
15.m: of one upon whom descent of power has fallen; this is the command declared by Śambhu. / The guru himself should perform the initiation of an impoverished person using his own wealth,

15.s:
api dūrvāmbubhiryadvā dīkṣāyai bhikṣate śiśuḥ /
bhikṣopāttaṃ nijaṃ vātha dhanaṃ prāggurave śiśuḥ // 37
15.d:
अपि दूर्वाम्बुभिर्यद्वा दीक्षायै भिक्षते शिशुः ।
भिक्षोपात्तं निजं वाथ धनं प्राग्गुरवे शिशुः ॥ 37
15.m: or even with dūrvā grass and water; or the child [disciple] begs for the sake of initiation. / The child first offers to the guru the wealth obtained by begging or his own [wealth],

15.s:
dadyādyena viśuddhaṃ tadyāgayogyatvamaśnute /
tatrādau śivatāpattisvātantryāveśa eva yaḥ // 38
15.d:
दद्याद्येन विशुद्धं तद्यागयोग्यत्वमश्नुते ।
तत्रादौ शिवतापत्तिस्वातन्त्र्यावेश एव यः ॥ 38
15.m: so that, purified, it attains fitness for the sacrifice. / There, in the beginning, that which is the entry into the absolute autonomy of the attainment of Śiva-nature—

15.s:
sa eva hi guruḥ kāryastato'sau dīkṣaṇe kṣamaḥ /
śivatāveśitā cāsya bahūpāyā pradarśitā // 39
15.d:
स एव हि गुरुः कार्यस्ततोऽसौ दीक्षणे क्षमः ।
शिवतावेशिता चास्य बहूपाया प्रदर्शिता ॥ 39
15.m: he alone should indeed act as guru, and therefore he is competent to bestow initiation. / And his state of entry into Śiva-nature is shown to have many means.

15.s:
kramikā bāhyarūpā tu snānanyāsārcanādibhiḥ /
bahvīṣu tāsu tāsveṣa kriyāsu śivatāṃ hṛdi // 40
15.d:
क्रमिका बाह्यरूपा तु स्नानन्यासार्चनादिभिः ।
बह्वीषु तासु तास्वेष क्रियासु शिवतां हृदि ॥ 40
15.m: The sequential and external [means], however, is by means of bathing, ritual imposition, worship, and the like. / Firmly fixing Śiva-nature in his heart through those numerous diverse rites,

15.s:
saṃdadhaddṛḍhamabhyeti śivabhāvaṃ prasannadhīḥ /
śivībhūto yadyadicchettattatkartuṃ samīhate // 41
15.d:
संदधद्दृढमभ्येति शिवभावं प्रसन्नधीः ।
शिवीभूतो यद्यदिच्छेत्तत्तत्कर्तुं समीहते ॥ 41
15.m: the serene-minded [master] firmly attains the state of Śiva. / Having become Śiva, whatever he desires, that he strives to accomplish.

15.s:
śivābhimānitopāyo bāhyo heturna mokṣadaḥ /
śivo'yaṃ śiva evāsmītyevamācāryaśiṣyayoḥ // 42
15.d:
शिवाभिमानितोपायो बाह्यो हेतुर्न मोक्षदः ।
शिवोऽयं शिव एवास्मीत्येवमाचार्यशिष्ययोः ॥ 42
15.m: The external means consists in the conviction of being Śiva; it is not [itself] the cause that bestows liberation. / 'This [disciple] is Śiva, I myself am Śiva'—in this way, between master and disciple,

15.s:
hetutadvattayā dārḍhyābhimāno mocako hyaṇoḥ /
nādhyātmena vinā bāhyaṃ nādhyātmaṃ bāhyavarjitam // 43
15.d:
हेतुतद्वत्तया दार्ढ्याभिमानो मोचको ह्यणोः ।
नाध्यात्मेन विना बाह्यं नाध्यात्मं बाह्यवर्जितम् ॥ 43
15.m: the firm conviction by way of the cause and its possessor is what liberates the bound soul. / The external does not succeed without the internal, nor is the internal devoid of the external;

15.s:
siddhyejjñānakriyābhyāṃ taddvitīyaṃ saṃprakāśate /
śrībrahmayāmale deva iti tena nyarūpayat // 44
15.d:
सिद्ध्येज्ज्ञानक्रियाभ्यां तद्द्वितीयं संप्रकाशते ।
श्रीब्रह्मयामले देव इति तेन न्यरूपयत् ॥ 44
15.m: that second [reality] becomes manifest through knowledge and action. / The Lord explained this in the venerated Brahmayāmala:

15.s:
śrīmadānandaśāstre ca nāśuddhiḥ syādvipaścitaḥ /
kintu snānaṃ suvastratvaṃ tuṣṭisaṃjananaṃ bhavet // 45
15.d:
श्रीमदानन्दशास्त्रे च नाशुद्धिः स्याद्विपश्चितः ।
किन्तु स्नानं सुवस्त्रत्वं तुष्टिसंजननं भवेत् ॥ 45
15.m: "And in the venerated treatise of bliss: there can be no impurity for the wise one; / nevertheless, bathing and wearing fine garments generate contentment.

15.s:
tatra prasiddhadehādimātṛnirmalatākramāt /
ayatnato'ntarantaḥ syānnairmalya snāyatāṃ tataḥ // 46
15.d:
तत्र प्रसिद्धदेहादिमातृनिर्मलताक्रमात् ।
अयत्नतोऽन्तरन्तः स्यान्नैर्मल्य स्नायतां ततः ॥ 46
15.m: There, through the sequence of well-known purity of the body and other [knowing] subjects, / internal purity arises within without effort; therefore, let them bathe."

15.s:
snānaṃ ca devadevasya yanmūrtyaṣṭakamucyate /
tatraivaṃ mantradīpte'ntarmaladāhe nimajjanam // 47
15.d:
स्नानं च देवदेवस्य यन्मूर्त्यष्टकमुच्यते ।
तत्रैवं मन्त्रदीप्तेऽन्तर्मलदाहे निमज्जनम् ॥ 47
15.m: And the bathing is what is called the eightfold form of the God of gods; / there, immersion is the burning of internal impurities illuminated by mantras.

15.s:
tatreṣṭamantrahṛdayo gorajo'ntaḥ padatrayam /
gatvāgatya bhajetsnānaṃ pārthivaṃ dhṛtidāyakam // 48
15.d:
तत्रेष्टमन्त्रहृदयो गोरजोऽन्तः पदत्रयम् ।
गत्वागत्य भजेत्स्नानं पार्थिवं धृतिदायकम् ॥ 48
15.m: There, with the heart-formula of his chosen deity, walking and returning three paces within cow-dust, / he should practice the earthly bath, which bestows stability.

15.s:
astramantritamṛddhūtamalaḥ pañcāṅgamantritaiḥ /
jalairmūrdhādipādāntaṃ kramādākṣālayettataḥ // 49
15.d:
अस्त्रमन्त्रितमृद्धूतमलः पञ्चाङ्गमन्त्रितैः ।
जलैर्मूर्धादिपादान्तं क्रमादाक्षालयेत्ततः ॥ 49
15.m: With dirt washed of impurity consecrated by the weapon-mantra, and with waters consecrated by the five ancillary mantras, / he should then wash himself successively from head to foot.

15.s:
nimajjetsāṅgamūlākhyaṃ japannā tanmayatvataḥ /
utthāyāśeṣasajjyotirdevatāgarbhamambare // 50
15.d:
निमज्जेत्साङ्गमूलाख्यं जपन्ना तन्मयत्वतः ।
उत्थायाशेषसज्ज्योतिर्देवतागर्भमम्बरे ॥ 50
15.m: He should immerse himself, reciting the principal mantra along with its ancillaries, until identity with it is reached. / Rising up, in the sky, [he should behold] the sun containing all radiant deities within its womb;

15.s:
sūryaṃ jalena mālinyā tarpayedviśvatarpakam /
devānpitṝnmunīnyakṣān rakṣāṃsyanyacca bhautikam // 51
15.d:
सूर्यं जलेन मालिन्या तर्पयेद्विश्वतर्पकम् ।
देवान्पितॄन्मुनीन्यक्षान् रक्षांस्यन्यच्च भौतिकम् ॥ 51
15.m: with water [reciting] Mālinī, he should satisfy the sun that satisfies all: / the gods, ancestors, sages, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and other elemental beings.

15.s:
sarvaṃ saṃtarpayetprāṇo vīryātmā sa ca bhāskaraḥ /
tato japetparāmekāṃ prāguktoccārayogataḥ // 52
15.d:
सर्वं संतर्पयेत्प्राणो वीर्यात्मा स च भास्करः ।
ततो जपेत्परामेकां प्रागुक्तोच्चारयोगतः ॥ 52
15.m: He should satisfy everything; and that sun is the vital breath, whose nature is potency. / Then he should recite the single supreme [mantra] through the union of utterance stated before.

15.s:
ā tanmayatvasaṃvitterjalasnānamidaṃ matam /
agnyutthaṃ bhasma śastreṇa japtvā malanivarhaṇam // 53
15.d:
आ तन्मयत्वसंवित्तेर्जलस्नानमिदं मतम् ।
अग्न्युत्थं भस्म शस्त्रेण जप्त्वा मलनिवर्हणम् ॥ 53
15.m: This is considered the water-bath, lasting until the consciousness of identity with it [is achieved]. / Having recited the weapon-mantra over fire-born ash which eliminates impurity,

15.s:
kavaktrahṛdguhyapade pañcāṅgairbhasma mantritam /
bhasmamuṣṭiṃ sāṅgamūlajaptāṃ mūrdhni kṣipettataḥ // 54
15.d:
कवक्त्रहृद्गुह्यपदे पञ्चाङ्गैर्भस्म मन्त्रितम् ।
भस्ममुष्टिं साङ्गमूलजप्तां मूर्ध्नि क्षिपेत्ततः ॥ 54
15.m: ash consecrated with the five ancillaries [is applied] to the head, face, heart, secret organ, and feet; / then he should cast upon his head a handful of ash recited over with the principal mantra and ancillaries.

15.s:
hastapādau jalenaiva prakṣālyācamanādikam /
tarpaṇaṃ japa ityevaṃ bhasmasnānaṃ hi taijasam // 55
15.d:
हस्तपादौ जलेनैव प्रक्षाल्याचमनादिकम् ।
तर्पणं जप इत्येवं भस्मस्नानं हि तैजसम् ॥ 55
15.m: Washing hands and feet with water, sipping water, / offering libation, and recitation—such is the fiery bath of ash.

15.s:
gorajovatyanudrikte vāyau hlādini mantravāk /
gatyāgatiprayoge vā vāyavyaṃ snānamācaret // 56
15.d:
गोरजोवत्यनुद्रिक्ते वायौ ह्लादिनि मन्त्रवाक् ।
गत्यागतिप्रयोगे वा वायव्यं स्नानमाचरेत् ॥ 56
15.m: When the wind blows moderately like cow-dust, bringing delight, the mantric speaker / should perform the aerial bath, or through the practice of the movement of inhalation and exhalation.

15.s:
amale gagane vyāpinyekāgrībhūtadṛṣṭikaḥ /
smaranmantraṃ yadāsīta kānyā nirmalatā tataḥ // 57
15.d:
अमले गगने व्यापिन्येकाग्रीभूतदृष्टिकः ।
स्मरन्मन्त्रं यदासीत कान्या निर्मलता ततः ॥ 57
15.m: With gaze focused on the pure, all-pervasive sky, / when one sits remembering the mantra, what other purity could there be than that?

15.s:
yadi vā nirmalādvyomnaḥ patatā vāriṇā tanum /
sparśayenmantrajapayuṅ nābhasaṃ snānamīdṛśam // 58
15.d:
यदि वा निर्मलाद्व्योम्नः पतता वारिणा तनुम् ।
स्पर्शयेन्मन्त्रजपयुङ् नाभसं स्नानमीदृशम् ॥ 58
15.m: Or, joined with mantra recitation, one touches one's body with water falling from the pure sky; / such is the ethereal bath.

15.s:
evaṃ somārkatejaḥsu śivabhāvena bhāvanāt /
nimajjandhautamālinyaḥ kva vā yogyo na jāyate // 59
15.d:
एवं सोमार्कतेजःसु शिवभावेन भावनात् ।
निमज्जन्धौतमालिन्यः क्व वा योग्यो न जायते ॥ 59
15.m: Thus, by meditating with the attitude of Śiva on the splendors of moon, sun, and fire, / immersing himself and washing away dirt, where does he not become qualified?

15.s:
ātmaiva parameśāno nirācāramahāhradaḥ /
viśvaṃ nimajjya tatraiva tiṣṭhecchuddhaśca śodhakaḥ // 60
15.d:
आत्मैव परमेशानो निराचारमहाह्रदः ।
विश्वं निमज्ज्य तत्रैव तिष्ठेच्छुद्धश्च शोधकः ॥ 60
15.m: The Self itself is the supreme Lord, the great pool free of conventional rules; / having immersed the universe right there, he remains both pure and the purifier.

15.s:
iti snānāṣṭakaṃ śuddhāvuttarottaramuttamam /
sarvatra paścāttaṃ mantramekībhūtamupāharet // 61
15.d:
इति स्नानाष्टकं शुद्धावुत्तरोत्तरमुत्तमम् ।
सर्वत्र पश्चात्तं मन्त्रमेकीभूतमुपाहरेत् ॥ 61
15.m: Thus the group of eight baths is progressively superior in purification. / Everywhere, he should subsequently apply that mantra integrated into oneness.

15.s:
ghṛtyāpyāyamalaploṣavīryavyāptimṛjisthitīḥ /
abhedaṃ ca kramādeti snānāṣṭakaparo muniḥ // 62
15.d:
घृत्याप्यायमलप्लोषवीर्यव्याप्तिमृजिस्थितीः ।
अभेदं च क्रमादेति स्नानाष्टकपरो मुनिः ॥ 62
15.m: Endurance, nourishment, burning of impurity, potency, pervasion, cleanliness, stability, / and non-duality—the sage devoted to the group of eight baths attains these in sequence.

15.s:
etā hyanugrahātmāno mūrtayo'ṣṭau śivātmikāḥ /
svarūpaśivarūpābhyāṃ dhyānāttattatphalapradāḥ // 63
15.d:
एता ह्यनुग्रहात्मानो मूर्तयोऽष्टौ शिवात्मिकाः ।
स्वरूपशिवरूपाभ्यां ध्यानात्तत्तत्फलप्रदाः ॥ 63
15.m: For these eight forms, whose essence is Śiva, consist of grace; / through meditation on their own form and the form of Śiva, they bestow their respective fruits.

15.s:
anena vidhinārcāyāṃ kandādhārādiyojanām /
kurvanvyāsasamāsābhyāṃ dharādestatphalaṃ bhajet // 64
15.d:
अनेन विधिनार्चायां कन्दाधारादियोजनाम् ।
कुर्वन्व्याससमासाभ्यां धरादेस्तत्फलं भजेत् ॥ 64
15.m: In worship according to this rule, performing the integration of the bulb, base, and so forth / in extensive and concise forms, one attains that fruit of earth and the other [elements].

15.s:
tathāhi yogasaṃcāre mantrāḥ syurbhuvi pārthivāḥ /
āpye āpyā yāvadamī śive śivamayā iti // 65
15.d:
तथाहि योगसंचारे मन्त्राः स्युर्भुवि पार्थिवाः ।
आप्ये आप्या यावदमी शिवे शिवमया इति ॥ 65
15.m: For in the Yogasaṃcāra [it is said]: 'On earth, mantras are earthly; / in water, watery; up to: in Śiva, they consist of Śiva.'

15.s:
śrīnirmaryādaśāstre'pi taditthaṃ sunirūpitam /
dharādeśca viśeṣo'sti vīrasādhakasaṃmataḥ // 66
15.d:
श्रीनिर्मर्यादशास्त्रेऽपि तदित्थं सुनिरूपितम् ।
धरादेश्च विशेषोऽस्ति वीरसाधकसंमतः ॥ 66
15.m: In the venerated Nirmaryādaśāstra also it is well explained thus: / there is a special application of earth and the rest agreed upon by heroic adepts:

15.s:
raṇareṇurvīrajalaṃ vīrabhasma mahāmarut /
śmaśānāraṇyagaganaṃ candrārkau tadupāhitau // 67
15.d:
रणरेणुर्वीरजलं वीरभस्म महामरुत् ।
श्मशानारण्यगगनं चन्द्रार्कौ तदुपाहितौ ॥ 67
15.m: battle-dust, heroic water, heroic ash, a great storm, / cremation ground, forest, sky, the moon and sun situated there,

15.s:
ātmā nirdhūtaniḥśeṣavikalpātaṅkasusthitaḥ /
snānārcādāvityupāsyaṃ vīrāṇāṃ vigrahāṣṭakam // 68
15.d:
आत्मा निर्धूतनिःशेषविकल्पातङ्कसुस्थितः ।
स्नानार्चादावित्युपास्यं वीराणां विग्रहाष्टकम् ॥ 68
15.m: and the Self well-established with all affliction of conceptual construct shaken off: / this eightfold embodiment of heroes is to be worshipped in bathing, adoration, and the like.

15.s:
śrīmantriśirasi proktaṃ madyaśīdhusurādinā /
susvādunā prasannena tanunā susugandhinā // 69
15.d:
श्रीमन्त्रिशिरसि प्रोक्तं मद्यशीधुसुरादिना ।
सुस्वादुना प्रसन्नेन तनुना सुसुगन्धिना ॥ 69
15.m: In the venerated Mantriśiras it is taught that with liquor, rum, spirits, and the like, / delicious, clear, subtle, very fragrant,

15.s:
kandalādigatenāntarbahiḥ saṃskārapañcakam /
kṛtvā nirīkṣaṇaṃ prokṣya tāḍanāpyāyaguṇṭhanam // 70
15.d:
कन्दलादिगतेनान्तर्बहिः संस्कारपञ्चकम् ।
कृत्वा निरीक्षणं प्रोक्ष्य ताडनाप्यायगुण्ठनम् ॥ 70
15.m: situated in the root and other [centers] internally and externally, having performed the fivefold preparation— / gazing, sprinkling, striking, nourishing, and veiling—

15.s:
mantracakrasya tanmadhye pūjāṃ vipruṭpratarpaṇam /
tenātmasekaḥ kalaśamudrayā cābhiṣecanam // 71
15.d:
मन्त्रचक्रस्य तन्मध्ये पूजां विप्रुट्प्रतर्पणम् ।
तेनात्मसेकः कलशमुद्रया चाभिषेचनम् ॥ 71
15.m: and worship of the circle of mantras within it, offering satiation drop by drop, / anointing oneself with it and consecrated sprinkling with the water-pot gesture,

15.s:
devatātarpaṇaṃ dehaprāṇobhayapathāśritam /
sarvatīrthatapoyajñadānādi phalamaśnute // 72
15.d:
देवतातर्पणं देहप्राणोभयपथाश्रितम् ।
सर्वतीर्थतपोयज्ञदानादि फलमश्नुते ॥ 72
15.m: and satisfying the deities supported on both paths of body and breath, / one enjoys the fruit of all sacred fords, austerities, sacrifices, charitable gifts, and the rest.

15.s:
madyasnāne sādhakendro mumukṣuḥ kevalībhavet /
yataḥ śivamayaṃ madyaṃ sarve mantrāḥ śivodbhavāḥ // 73
15.d:
मद्यस्नाने साधकेन्द्रो मुमुक्षुः केवलीभवेत् ।
यतः शिवमयं मद्यं सर्वे मन्त्राः शिवोद्भवाः ॥ 73
15.m: In the bath of liquor, the king of adepts desiring liberation becomes isolated [in pure consciousness], / because liquor consists of Śiva and all mantras originate from Śiva.

15.s:
śivaśaktyorna bhedo'sti śaktyutthāstu marīcayaḥ /
tāsāmānandajanakaṃ madyaṃ śivamayaṃ tataḥ // 74
15.d:
शिवशक्त्योर्न भेदोऽस्ति शक्त्युत्थास्तु मरीचयः ।
तासामानन्दजनकं मद्यं शिवमयं ततः ॥ 74
15.m: There is no difference between Śiva and Śakti, while the rays [of consciousness] arise from Śakti; / liquor generates their bliss, and therefore consists of Śiva.

15.s:
prabuddhe saṃvidaḥ pūrṇe rūpe'dhikṛtibhājanam /
mantradhyānasamādhānabhedātsnānaṃ tu yanna tat // 75
15.d:
प्रबुद्धे संविदः पूर्णे रूपेऽधिकृतिभाजनम् ।
मन्त्रध्यानसमाधानभेदात्स्नानं तु यन्न तत् ॥ 75
15.m: When consciousness is awakened into its full form, it is the vessel of qualification. / But the bathing that is differentiated by mantra, meditation, and concentration is not that.

15.s:
yuktaṃ snānaṃ yato nyāsakarmādau yogyatāvaham /
asya snānāṣṭakasyāsti bāhyāntaratayā dvitā // 76
15.d:
युक्तं स्नानं यतो न्यासकर्मादौ योग्यतावहम् ।
अस्य स्नानाष्टकस्यास्ति बाह्यान्तरतया द्विता ॥ 76
15.m: Yet bathing is appropriate because it brings qualification for the rite of ritual imposition and the like. / This group of eight baths is twofold, being external and internal.

15.s:
āntaraṃ tadyathordhvendudhārāmṛtapariplavaḥ /
yato randhrordhvagāḥ sārdhamaṅgulaṃ vyāpya saṃsthitāḥ // 77
15.d:
आन्तरं तद्यथोर्ध्वेन्दुधारामृतपरिप्लवः ।
यतो रन्ध्रोर्ध्वगाः सार्धमङ्गुलं व्याप्य संस्थिताः ॥ 77
15.m: The internal [bath] is as follows: the overflowing nectar of the stream from the upper moon, / because [the streams] rising above the cranial aperture abide pervading half an inch.

15.s:
mūrtayo'ṣṭāvapi proktāḥ pratyekaṃ dvādaśāntataḥ /
eṣāmekatamaṃ snānaṃ kuryāddvitryādiśo'pivā // 78
15.d:
मूर्तयोऽष्टावपि प्रोक्ताः प्रत्येकं द्वादशान्ततः ।
एषामेकतमं स्नानं कुर्याद्द्वित्र्यादिशोऽपिवा ॥ 78
15.m: All eight forms too are declared [to flow] each from the dvādaśānta; / one may perform any one of these baths, or in groups of two, three, and so forth. // 78

15.s:
iti snānavidhiḥ prokto bhairaveṇāmalīkṛtau /
snānānantarakartavyamathedamupadiśyate // 79
15.d:
इति स्नानविधिः प्रोक्तो भैरवेणामलीकृतौ ।
स्नानानन्तरकर्तव्यमथेदमुपदिश्यते ॥ 79
15.m: Thus has the rite of bathing been taught by Bhairava for the sake of purification. / Now the duty to be done immediately after bathing is taught: // 79

15.s:
bhāvaṃ prasannamālocya vrajedyāgagṛhaṃ tataḥ /
parvatāgranadītīraikaliṅgādi yaducyate // 80
15.d:
भावं प्रसन्नमालोच्य व्रजेद्यागगृहं ततः ।
पर्वताग्रनदीतीरैकलिङ्गादि यदुच्यते ॥ 80
15.m: Having observed that his disposition is serene, he should then go to the house of sacrifice. / What is spoken of as a mountain peak, a riverbank, a solitary liṅga, and so forth, // 80

15.s:
tadbāhyamiha tatsiddhiviśeṣāya na muktaye /
ābhyantaraṃ nagāgrādi dehāntaḥ prāṇayojanam // 81
15.d:
तद्बाह्यमिह तत्सिद्धिविशेषाय न मुक्तये ।
आभ्यन्तरं नगाग्रादि देहान्तः प्राणयोजनम् ॥ 81
15.m: is external here, [intended] for special spiritual accomplishments, not for liberation. / The internal mountain peak and the like is the application of the vital breath within the body; // 81

15.s:
sādhakānāmupāyaḥ syātsiddhaye natu muktaye /
pīṭhasthānaṃ sadā yāgayogyaṃ śāstreṣu bhaṇyate // 82
15.d:
साधकानामुपायः स्यात्सिद्धये नतु मुक्तये ।
पीठस्थानं सदा यागयोग्यं शास्त्रेषु भण्यते ॥ 82
15.m: it serves as a means for adepts toward spiritual accomplishment, but not for liberation. / A sacred seat is always said in the scriptures to be suitable for sacrifice, // 82

15.s:
tacca bāhyāntarādrūpādbahirdehe ca susphuṭam /
yataḥ śrīnaiśasañcāre parameśo nyarūpayat // 83
15.d:
तच्च बाह्यान्तराद्रूपाद्बहिर्देहे च सुस्फुटम् ।
यतः श्रीनैशसञ्चारे परमेशो न्यरूपयत् ॥ 83
15.m: and that is very clear from its internal and external nature, both outside and in the body; / for in the venerable Naiśasañcāra, the Supreme Lord explained: // 83

15.s:
tasyecchā pīṭhamādhāro yatrasthaṃ sacarācaram /
agryaṃ tatkāmarūpaṃ syādbindunādadvayaṃ tataḥ // 84
15.d:
तस्येच्छा पीठमाधारो यत्रस्थं सचराचरम् ।
अग्र्यं तत्कामरूपं स्याद्बिन्दुनादद्वयं ततः ॥ 84
15.m: "Her will is the seat, the foundation upon which stands all that moves and is still; / that is the foremost Kāmarūpa. Then the pair of point and resonance: // 84

15.s:
nādapīṭhaṃ pūrṇagirirdakṣiṇe vāmataḥ punaḥ /
pīṭhamuḍḍayanaṃ bindurmukhyaṃ pīṭhatrayaṃ tvidam // 85
15.d:
नादपीठं पूर्णगिरिर्दक्षिणे वामतः पुनः ।
पीठमुड्डयनं बिन्दुर्मुख्यं पीठत्रयं त्विदम् ॥ 85
15.m: Pūrṇagiri is the seat of resonance on the right, and on the left again / is the seat Uḍḍayana, the point. These, however, are the three primary seats; // 85

15.s:
jñeyaṃ saṃkalpanārūpamardhapīṭhamataḥ param /
śāktaṃ kuṇḍalinī vedakalaṃ ca tryupapīṭhakam // 86
15.d:
ज्ञेयं संकल्पनारूपमर्धपीठमतः परम् ।
शाक्तं कुण्डलिनी वेदकलं च त्र्युपपीठकम् ॥ 86
15.m: they are to be known as conceptual ideation. Beyond this is the half-seat: / it belongs to the Śakti, is Kuṇḍalinī, and [has the nature of] the four Vedas. And there are three secondary seats: // 86

15.s:
devīkoṭṭojjayinyau dve tathā kulagiriḥ paraḥ /
lālanaṃ baindavaṃ vyāptiriti saṃdohakatrayam // 87
15.d:
देवीकोट्टोज्जयिन्यौ द्वे तथा कुलगिरिः परः ।
लालनं बैन्दवं व्याप्तिरिति संदोहकत्रयम् ॥ 87
15.m: Devīkoṭṭa and Ujjayinī, and further, the Kulagiri; / Lālana, Baindava, and Vyāpti: this is the triad of gatherings; // 87

15.s:
puṇḍravardhanavārendre tathaikāmramidaṃ bahiḥ /
navadhā kathitaṃ pīṭhamantarbāhyakrameṇa tat // 88
15.d:
पुण्ड्रवर्धनवारेन्द्रे तथैकाम्रमिदं बहिः ।
नवधा कथितं पीठमन्तर्बाह्यक्रमेण तत् ॥ 88
15.m: Puṇḍravardhana, Vārendra, and this Ekāmra are outside." / Thus the seat is declared to be ninefold, according to the internal and external order. // 88

15.s:
kṣetrāṣṭakaṃ kṣetravido hṛdambhojadalāṣṭakam /
prayāgo varaṇā paścādaṭṭahāso jayantikā // 89
15.d:
क्षेत्राष्टकं क्षेत्रविदो हृदम्भोजदलाष्टकम् ।
प्रयागो वरणा पश्चादट्टहासो जयन्तिका ॥ 89
15.m: Those who know the sacred field [regard] the eightfold field as the eight petals of the heart lotus: / Prayāga, Varaṇā, then Aṭṭahāsa, Jayantikā, // 89

15.s:
vārāṇasī ca kāliṅgaṃ kulūtā lāhulā tathā /
upakṣetrāṣṭakaṃ prāhurhṛtpadmāgradalāṣṭakam // 90
15.d:
वाराणसी च कालिङ्गं कुलूता लाहुला तथा ।
उपक्षेत्राष्टकं प्राहुर्हृत्पद्माग्रदलाष्टकम् ॥ 90
15.m: Vārāṇasī, Kāliṅga, and likewise Kulūtā and Lāhulā. / They declare the eight secondary fields to be the tips of the eight petals of the heart lotus: // 90

15.s:
virajairuḍikā hālā elā pūḥ kṣīrikā purī /
māyākhyā marudeśaśca bāhyābhyantararūpataḥ // 91
15.d:
विरजैरुडिका हाला एला पूः क्षीरिका पुरी ।
मायाख्या मरुदेशश्च बाह्याभ्यन्तररूपतः ॥ 91
15.m: Virajā, Eruḍikā, Hālā, Elāpūr, Kṣīrikā-purī, / Māyākhyā, and the Maru country, in terms of both external and internal nature. // 91

15.s:
hṛtpadmadalasandhīnāmupasaṃdohakāṣṭatā /
jālandharaṃ ca naipālaṃ kaśmīrā gargikā haraḥ // 92
15.d:
हृत्पद्मदलसन्धीनामुपसंदोहकाष्टता ।
जालन्धरं च नैपालं कश्मीरा गर्गिका हरः ॥ 92
15.m: The eight junctions of the petals of the heart lotus constitute the eight secondary gatherings: / Jālandhara, Nepāla, Kaśmīra, Gargikā, Hara, // 92

15.s:
mlecchadigdvāravṛttiśca kurukṣetraṃ ca kheṭakam /
dvipathaṃ dvayasaṃghaṭṭāttripathaṃ trayamelakāt // 93
15.d:
म्लेच्छदिग्द्वारवृत्तिश्च कुरुक्षेत्रं च खेटकम् ।
द्विपथं द्वयसंघट्टात्त्रिपथं त्रयमेलकात् ॥ 93
15.m: the region of the borderlands of the barbarians, Kurukṣetra, and Kheṭaka. / A crossroad of two paths arises from the union of two; a crossroad of three paths, from the conjunction of three; // 93

15.s:
catuṣpathaṃ śaktimato layāttatraiva manvate /
nāsāntatālurandhrāntametaddehe vyavasthitam // 94
15.d:
चतुष्पथं शक्तिमतो लयात्तत्रैव मन्वते ।
नासान्ततालुरन्ध्रान्तमेतद्देहे व्यवस्थितम् ॥ 94
15.m: they consider a crossroad of four paths [to arise] from the dissolution of the possessor of power in that very place. / Located in the body, this extends from the tip of the nose to the palatal aperture. // 94

15.s:
bhrūmadhyakaṇṭhahṛtsaṃjñaṃ madhyamaṃ tadudāhṛtam /
nābhikandamahānandadhāma tatkaulikaṃ trayam // 95
15.d:
भ्रूमध्यकण्ठहृत्संज्ञं मध्यमं तदुदाहृतम् ।
नाभिकन्दमहानन्दधाम तत्कौलिकं त्रयम् ॥ 95
15.m: The intermediate [triad] is spoken of as called the eyebrow center, throat, and heart; / the navel, bulb, and the abode of great bliss are the Kaula triad. // 95

15.s:
parvatāgraṃ nadītīramekaliṅgaṃ tadeva ca /
kiṃ vātibahunā sarvaṃ saṃvittau prāṇagaṃ tataḥ // 96
15.d:
पर्वताग्रं नदीतीरमेकलिङ्गं तदेव च ।
किं वातिबहुना सर्वं संवित्तौ प्राणगं ततः ॥ 96
15.m: Mountain peak, riverbank, and solitary liṅga are that very thing. / Or what need is there of saying much? Everything is situated in consciousness, then in the vital breath, // 96

15.s:
tato dehasthitaṃ tasmāddehāyatanago bhavet /
bāhye tu tādṛśāntaḥsthayogamārgaviśāradāḥ // 97
15.d:
ततो देहस्थितं तस्माद्देहायतनगो भवेत् ।
बाह्ये तु तादृशान्तःस्थयोगमार्गविशारदाः ॥ 97
15.m: then positioned in the body; from that, one should go to the house of the body. / But externally, goddesses skilled in such an internal path of yoga / are born spontaneously; that is called an external sacred seat. // 97

15.s:
devyaḥ svabhāvājjāyante pīṭhaṃ tadvāhyamucyate /
yathā svabhāvato mlecchā adharmapathavartinaḥ // 98
15.d:
देव्यः स्वभावाज्जायन्ते पीठं तद्वाह्यमुच्यते ।
यथा स्वभावतो म्लेच्छा अधर्मपथवर्तिनः ॥ 98
15.m: Just as barbarians by their very nature tread the path of unrighteousness / in that land, so by cosmic order knowledge and yoga reside in certain places. // 98

15.s:
tatra deśe niyatyetthaṃ jñānayogau sthitau kvacit /
yathācātanmayo'pyeti pāpitāṃ taiḥ samāgamāt // 99
15.d:
तत्र देशे नियत्येत्थं ज्ञानयोगौ स्थितौ क्वचित् ।
यथाचातन्मयोऽप्येति पापितां तैः समागमात् ॥ 99
15.m: And just as one who does not share that nature falls into sin through contact with them, // 99

15.s:
tathā pīṭhasthito'pyeti jñānayogādipātratām /
mukhyatvena śarīre'ntaḥ prāṇe saṃvidi paśyataḥ // 100
15.d:
तथा पीठस्थितोऽप्येति ज्ञानयोगादिपात्रताम् ।
मुख्यत्वेन शरीरेऽन्तः प्राणे संविदि पश्यतः ॥ 100
15.m: so one residing in a sacred seat becomes a fit vessel for knowledge, yoga, and the like. / For one who sees this universe primarily within the body, in the vital breath, and in consciousness, / what use are the other ostentatious displays of wandering outside? // 100

15.s:
viśvametatkimanyaiḥ syādbahirbhramaṇaḍambaraiḥ /
ityevamantarbāhye ca tattaccakraphalārthinām // 101
15.d:
विश्वमेतत्किमन्यैः स्याद्बहिर्भ्रमणडम्बरैः ।
इत्येवमन्तर्बाह्ये च तत्तच्चक्रफलार्थिनाम् ॥ 101
15.m: Thus, externally and internally, for those desiring the fruits of the various wheels, // 101

15.s:
sthānabhedo vicitraśca sa śāstre saṃkhyayojjhitaḥ /
śrīvīrāvalihṛdaye sapta sthānāni śaktikamalayugam // 102
15.d:
स्थानभेदो विचित्रश्च स शास्त्रे संख्ययोज्झितः ।
श्रीवीरावलिहृदये सप्त स्थानानि शक्तिकमलयुगम् ॥ 102
15.m: the diversity of places is manifold and is beyond number in the scripture. / In the venerable Vīrāvalīhṛdaya there are seven places: the pair of Śakti lotuses, // 102

15.s:
surapathacatuṣpathākhyaśmaśānamekāntaśūnyavṛkṣau ca /
iti nirvacanaguṇasthityupacāradṛśā vibodha evoktaḥ // 103
15.d:
सुरपथचतुष्पथाख्यश्मशानमेकान्तशून्यवृक्षौ च ।
इति निर्वचनगुणस्थित्युपचारदृशा विबोध एवोक्तः ॥ 103
15.m: the road of the gods, the crossroad of four paths, the cremation ground, the solitary void, and the tree. / Awakening alone is thus spoken of from the perspective of metaphorical usage based on etymology and the state of attributes. // 103

15.s:
tadadhiṣṭhite ca cakre śārīre bahiratho bhavedyāgaḥ /
muktaye tanna yāgasya sthānabhedaḥ prakalpyate // 104
15.d:
तदधिष्ठिते च चक्रे शारीरे बहिरथो भवेद्यागः ।
मुक्तये तन्न यागस्य स्थानभेदः प्रकल्प्यते ॥ 104
15.m: And in the bodily wheel presided over by that, sacrifice may take place externally. / For liberation, however, distinction among places of sacrifice is not prescribed, // 104

15.s:
deśopāyā na sā yasmātsā hi bhāvaprasādataḥ /
uktaṃ ca śrīniśācāre siddhisādhanakāṅkṣiṇām // 105
15.d:
देशोपाया न सा यस्मात्सा हि भावप्रसादतः ।
उक्तं च श्रीनिशाचारे सिद्धिसाधनकाङ्क्षिणाम् ॥ 105
15.m: since liberation does not have external place as its means, because it arises from serenity of mind. / And it is said in the venerable Niśācāra: "For those who desire the accomplishment of siddhis // 105

15.s:
sthānaṃ mumukṣuṇā tyājyaṃ sarpakañcukavattvidam /
muktirna sthānajanitā yadā śrotrapathaṃ gatam // 106
15.d:
स्थानं मुमुक्षुणा त्याज्यं सर्पकञ्चुकवत्त्विदम् ।
मुक्तिर्न स्थानजनिता यदा श्रोत्रपथं गतम् ॥ 106
15.m: a place [is prescribed]; but a seeker of liberation should abandon this like a serpent's slough. / Liberation is not produced by a place: when the reality taught by the guru / has reached the path of hearing, // 106

15.s:
gurostattvaṃ tadā muktistaddārḍhyāya tu pūjanam /
yatra yatra hṛdambhojaṃ vikāsaṃ pratipadyate // 107
15.d:
गुरोस्तत्त्वं तदा मुक्तिस्तद्दार्ढ्याय तु पूजनम् ।
यत्र यत्र हृदम्भोजं विकासं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 107
15.m: liberation is attained then and there, whereas worship is for its firm consolidation." / Wherever the lotus of the heart unfolds, // 107

15.s:
tatraiva dhāmni bāhye'ntaryāgaśrīḥ pratitiṣṭhati /
nānyatragatyā mokṣo'sti so'jñānagranthikartanāt // 108
15.d:
तत्रैव धाम्नि बाह्येऽन्तर्यागश्रीः प्रतितिष्ठति ।
नान्यत्रगत्या मोक्षोऽस्ति सोऽज्ञानग्रन्थिकर्तनात् ॥ 108
15.m: in that very abode, outside or inside, the splendor of sacrifice is established. / Liberation does not come about by going elsewhere; it comes from severing the knot of ignorance, // 108

15.s:
tacca saṃvidvikāsena śrīmadvīrāvalīpade /
guravastu vimuktau vā siddhau vā vimalā matiḥ // 109
15.d:
तच्च संविद्विकासेन श्रीमद्वीरावलीपदे ।
गुरवस्तु विमुक्तौ वा सिद्धौ वा विमला मतिः ॥ 109
15.m: and that arises through the unfolding of consciousness. In the context of the venerable Vīrāvalī, / the masters, however, state that a pure mind is the cause // 109

15.s:
heturityubhayatrāpi yāgauko yanmanoramam /
niyatiprāṇatāyogātsāmagrītastu yadyapi // 110
15.d:
हेतुरित्युभयत्रापि यागौको यन्मनोरमम् ।
नियतिप्राणतायोगात्सामग्रीतस्तु यद्यपि ॥ 110
15.m: either in liberation or in spiritual accomplishment; therefore, in both cases, the sacrifice house is that which is pleasing to the mind. / Even though, through the combination of ritual requisites conditioned by cosmic order, // 110

15.s:
siddhayo bhāvavaimalyaṃ tathāpi nikhilottamam /
vimalībhūtahṛdayo yattatra pratibimbayet // 111
15.d:
सिद्धयो भाववैमल्यं तथापि निखिलोत्तमम् ।
विमलीभूतहृदयो यत्तत्र प्रतिबिम्बयेत् ॥ 111
15.m: spiritual accomplishments [may arise], purity of disposition is nevertheless the highest of all. / Whatever that [practitioner] whose heart has become purified should reflect upon there, // 111

15.s:
sādhyaṃ tadasya dārḍhyena saphalatvāya kalpate /
uktaṃ śrīsāraśāstre ca nirvikalpo hi sidhyati // 112
15.d:
साध्यं तदस्य दार्ढ्येन सफलत्वाय कल्पते ।
उक्तं श्रीसारशास्त्रे च निर्विकल्पो हि सिध्यति ॥ 112
15.m: that object to be attained serves for success through its firmness. / And it is said in the venerable Sāraśāstra: "The one free from conceptual constructs indeed attains accomplishment, // 112

15.s:
kliśyante savikalpāstu kalpokte'pi kṛte sati /
tadākramya balaṃ mantrā ayamevodayaḥ sphuṭaḥ // 113
15.d:
क्लिश्यन्ते सविकल्पास्तु कल्पोक्तेऽपि कृते सति ।
तदाक्रम्य बलं मन्त्रा अयमेवोदयः स्फुटः ॥ 113
15.m: while those caught in conceptual constructs suffer, even when doing what is enjoined in the manuals." / "Having seized that power, the mantras..." and "This very awakening is clear..."— // 113

15.s:
ityādibhiḥ spandavākyairetadeva nirūpitam /
tasmātsiddhyai vimuktyai vā pūjājapasamādhiṣu // 114
15.d:
इत्यादिभिः स्पन्दवाक्यैरेतदेव निरूपितम् ।
तस्मात्सिद्ध्यै विमुक्त्यै वा पूजाजपसमाधिषु ॥ 114
15.m: by such verses of the Spanda, this very truth is demonstrated. / Therefore, whether for spiritual accomplishment or for liberation, in worship, recitation, and absorption, // 114

15.s:
tatsthānaṃ yatra viśrāntisundaraṃ hṛdayaṃ bhavet /
yāgaukaḥ prāpya śuddhātmā bahireva vyavasthitaḥ // 115
15.d:
तत्स्थानं यत्र विश्रान्तिसुन्दरं हृदयं भवेत् ।
यागौकः प्राप्य शुद्धात्मा बहिरेव व्यवस्थितः ॥ 115
15.m: that is the place where the heart becomes beautiful through rest. / Having reached the sacrificial house, the pure-souled one, remaining on the outside, // 115

15.s:
nyāsaṃ sāmānyataḥ kuryādbahiryāgaprasiddhaye /
mātṛkāṃ mālinīṃ vātha dvitayaṃ vā kramākramāt // 116
15.d:
न्यासं सामान्यतः कुर्याद्बहिर्यागप्रसिद्धये ।
मातृकां मालिनीं वाथ द्वितयं वा क्रमाक्रमात् ॥ 116
15.m: should perform the general installation for the accomplishment of the external sacrifice, / [imposing] the Mātṛkā or the Mālinī, or both, in sequential or non-sequential order, // 116

15.s:
sṛṣṭyapyayadvayaiḥ kuryādekaikaṃ saṃghaśo dviśaḥ /
lalāṭavaktre dṛkkarṇanāsāgaṇḍaradauṣṭhage // 117
15.d:
सृष्ट्यप्ययद्वयैः कुर्यादेकैकं संघशो द्विशः ।
ललाटवक्त्रे दृक्कर्णनासागण्डरदौष्ठगे ॥ 117
15.m: by means of both emanation and resorption, [installing] each phoneme singly or in groups, twice over: / On forehead and mouth, eyes, ears, nostrils, cheeks, teeth, and lips, // 117

15.s:
dvaye dvaye śikhājihve visargāntāstu ṣoḍaśa /
dakṣānyayoḥ skandhabāhukarāṅgulinakhe kacau // 118
15.d:
द्वये द्वये शिखाजिह्वे विसर्गान्तास्तु षोडश ।
दक्षान्ययोः स्कन्धबाहुकराङ्गुलिनखे कचौ ॥ 118
15.m: taken in pairs, on tuft and tongue: the sixteen [vowels] ending with visarga; / on right and left shoulder, arm, hand, finger, nail, hair; // 118

15.s:
vargau ṭatau kramātkaṭyāmūrvādiṣu niyojayet /
pavargaṃ pārśvayoḥ pṛṣṭhe jaṭhare hṛdyatho nava // 119
15.d:
वर्गौ टतौ क्रमात्कट्यामूर्वादिषु नियोजयेत् ।
पवर्गं पार्श्वयोः पृष्ठे जठरे हृद्यथो नव ॥ 119
15.m: one should assign the ṭa- and ta-series successively on the waist and thighs, and so forth, / the pa-series on the flanks, back, belly, and heart; then the nine [semivowels and sibilants] // 119

15.s:
tvagraktamāṃsasūtrāsthivasāśukrapurogamān /
ityeṣa mātṛkānyāso mālinyāstu nirūpyate // 120
15.d:
त्वग्रक्तमांससूत्रास्थिवसाशुक्रपुरोगमान् ।
इत्येष मातृकान्यासो मालिन्यास्तु निरूप्यते ॥ 120
15.m: beginning with skin, blood, flesh, fat-channels, bone, marrow, and semen. / Such is the installation of the Mātṛkā; now that of the Mālinī is described: // 120

15.s:
na śikhā ṛ ṝ ḷ ḷḷ ca śiromālā tha mastakam /
netrāṇi cordhve dho'nye ī ghrāṇaṃ mudre ṇu ṇū śrutī // 121
15.d:
न शिखा ऋ ॠ ऌ ऌऌ च शिरोमाला थ मस्तकम् ।
नेत्राणि चोर्ध्वे धोऽन्ये ई घ्राणं मुद्रे णु णू श्रुती ॥ 121
15.m: na on the crown-tuft; ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, and ḷḷ on the garland of the head; tha on the crown of the head; / the upper eyes and the lower eyes; ī on the nostrils; the two gestures; ṇu and ṇū on the ears; // 121

15.s:
bakavarga+i+ā vaktradantajihvāgiri kramāt /
vabhayāḥ kaṇṭhadakṣādiskandhayorbhujayorḍaḍhau // 122
15.d:
बकवर्ग+इ+आ वक्त्रदन्तजिह्वागिरि क्रमात् ।
वभयाः कण्ठदक्षादिस्कन्धयोर्भुजयोर्डढौ ॥ 122
15.m: the ba-series, ka-series, i, and ā on the mouth, teeth, and tongue-tip respectively; / va, bha, and ya on the throat, right and other shoulder; ḍa and ḍha on the arms; // 122

15.s:
ṭho hastayorjhañau śākhā jraṭau śūlakapālake /
pa hṛcchalau stanau kṣīramā sa jīvo visargayuk // 123
15.d:
ठो हस्तयोर्झञौ शाखा ज्रटौ शूलकपालके ।
प हृच्छलौ स्तनौ क्षीरमा स जीवो विसर्गयुक् ॥ 123
15.m: ṭha on the hands; jha and ña on the fingers; ja, ra, and ṭa on the trident and skull-bowl; / pa on the heart; cha and la on the breasts; milk; ā; sa is the soul endowed with creative emission. // 123

15.s:
prāṇo havarṇaḥ kathitaḥ ṣakṣāvudaranābhigau /
maśāntā kaṭiguhyoruyugmagā jānunī tathā // 124
15.d:
प्राणो हवर्णः कथितः षक्षावुदरनाभिगौ ।
मशान्ता कटिगुह्योरुयुग्मगा जानुनी तथा ॥ 124
15.m:
The letter 'ha' is declared to be the vital breath; 'ṣa' and 'kṣa' reside in the abdomen and navel;
[the letters] from 'ma' to 'śa' reside in the waist, the genitals, and the pair of thighs, and likewise the knees; // 124

15.s:
eaikārau tatparau tu jaṅghe caraṇagau daphau /
ityeṣā mālinī devī śaktimatkṣobhitā yataḥ // 125
15.d:
एऐकारौ तत्परौ तु जङ्घे चरणगौ दफौ ।
इत्येषा मालिनी देवी शक्तिमत्क्षोभिता यतः ॥ 125
15.m:
'e' and 'ai' are next, on the calves; 'da' and 'pha' are located on the feet.
In this way [she is] the goddess Mālinī, since, agitated by the possessor of power, // 125

15.s:
kṛtyāveśāttataḥ śāktī tanuḥ sā paramārthataḥ /
anyonyaṃ bījayonīnāṃ kṣobhādvaisargikodayāt // 126
15.d:
कृत्यावेशात्ततः शाक्ती तनुः सा परमार्थतः ।
अन्योन्यं बीजयोनीनां क्षोभाद्वैसर्गिकोदयात् ॥ 126
15.m:
and through entering into action, she is in the ultimate sense an embodiment of power.
Because of the mutual agitation of seeds and wombs arising from creative emission, // 126

15.s:
kāṃ kāṃ siddhiṃ na vitaretkiṃ vā nyūnaṃ na pūrayet /
yonibījārṇasāṃkaryaṃ bahudhā yadyapi sthitam // 127
15.d:
कां कां सिद्धिं न वितरेत्किं वा न्यूनं न पूरयेत् ।
योनिबीजार्णसांकर्यं बहुधा यद्यपि स्थितम् ॥ 127
15.m:
what accomplishment would she not bestow, or what deficiency would she not make full?
Even though the commingling of vowels and consonants occurs in many ways, // 127

15.s:
tathāpi nādiphānto'yaṃ kramo mukhyaḥ prakīrtitaḥ /
phakārādisamuccārānnakārānte'dhvamaṇḍalam // 128
15.d:
तथापि नादिफान्तोऽयं क्रमो मुख्यः प्रकीर्तितः ।
फकारादिसमुच्चारान्नकारान्तेऽध्वमण्डलम् ॥ 128
15.m:
nevertheless this order, beginning with 'na' and ending with 'pha', is proclaimed as primary.
From the sounding of 'pha' and so forth, up to 'na', having dissolved the sphere of the paths, // 128

15.s:
saṃhṛtya saṃvidyā pūrṇā sā śabdairvarṇyate katham /
ataḥ śāstreṣu bahudhā kulaputtalikādibhiḥ // 129
15.d:
संहृत्य संविद्या पूर्णा सा शब्दैर्वर्ण्यते कथम् ।
अतः शास्त्रेषु बहुधा कुलपुत्तलिकादिभिः ॥ 129
15.m:
how could she, full of consciousness, be described in words?
Hence in the scriptures she is celebrated in various ways through forms such as the Kula puppet, // 129

15.s:
bhedairgītā hi mukhyeyaṃ nādiphānteti mālinī /
śabdarāśerbhairavasya yānucchūnatayāntarī // 130
15.d:
भेदैर्गीता हि मुख्येयं नादिफान्तेति मालिनी ।
शब्दराशेर्भैरवस्य यानुच्छूनतयान्तरी ॥ 130
15.m:
yet this Mālinī, beginning with 'na' and ending with 'pha', is indeed primary.
Because she is inside Bhairava, who is the mass of sounds, in an swollen state, // 130

15.s:
sā māteva bhaviṣyattvāttenāsau mātṛkoditā /
mālinī mālitā rudrairdhārikā siddhimokṣayoḥ // 131
15.d:
सा मातेव भविष्यत्त्वात्तेनासौ मातृकोदिता ।
मालिनी मालिता रुद्रैर्धारिका सिद्धिमोक्षयोः ॥ 131
15.m:
and because she is about to become [everything] like a mother, she is called Mātṛkā.
Mālinī is garlanded by the Rudras, the upholder of accomplishment and liberation, // 131

15.s:
phaleṣu puṣpitā pūjyā saṃhāradhvaniṣaṭpadī /
saṃhāradānādānādiśaktiyuktā yato ralau // 132
15.d:
फलेषु पुष्पिता पूज्या संहारध्वनिषट्पदी ।
संहारदानादानादिशक्तियुक्ता यतो रलौ ॥ 132
15.m:
blossomed into fruits, worthy of worship, a female bee buzzing with the sound of resorption.
Because she is endowed with powers such as resorption, giving, and taking, and because 'ra' and 'la' // 132

15.s:
ekatvena smarantīti śaṃbhunātho nirūcivān /
śabdarāśirmālinī ca śivaśaktyātmakaṃ tvidam // 133
15.d:
एकत्वेन स्मरन्तीति शंभुनाथो निरूचिवान् ।
शब्दराशिर्मालिनी च शिवशक्त्यात्मकं त्विदम् ॥ 133
15.m:
are remembered as one, so Śambhunātha explained.
Both the mass of sounds and Mālinī consist of Śiva and power; // 133

15.s:
ekaikatrāpi pūrṇatvācchivaśaktisvabhāvatā /
tena bhraṣṭe vidhau vīrye svarūpe vānayā param // 134
15.d:
एकैकत्रापि पूर्णत्वाच्छिवशक्तिस्वभावता ।
तेन भ्रष्टे विधौ वीर्ये स्वरूपे वानया परम् ॥ 134
15.m:
due to fullness in each one, their nature is Śiva and power.
Therefore, when a ritual rule has failed, or its potency, or its essential nature, through her // 134

15.s:
mantrā nyastāḥ punarnyāsātpūryante tatphalapradāḥ /
uktaṃ śrīpūrvatantre ca viśeṣavidhihīnite // 135
15.d:
मन्त्रा न्यस्ताः पुनर्न्यासात्पूर्यन्ते तत्फलप्रदाः ।
उक्तं श्रीपूर्वतन्त्रे च विशेषविधिहीनिते ॥ 135
15.m:
the mantras imposed through this renewed imposition become complete and bestow their fruit.
And it is stated in the venerable Pūrvatantra: 'In what is devoid of specific injunctions, // 135

15.s:
nyasyecchāktaśarīrārthaṃ bhinnayoni tu mālinīm /
viśeṣaṇamidaṃ hetau hetvarthaśca nirūpitaḥ // 136
15.d:
न्यस्येच्छाक्तशरीरार्थं भिन्नयोनि तु मालिनीम् ।
विशेषणमिदं हेतौ हेत्वर्थश्च निरूपितः ॥ 136
15.m:
one should impose Mālinī, whose wombs are separated, for the sake of a body infused with power.'
This qualification serves as the cause, and the purpose of the cause has been explained: // 136

15.s:
yatheṣṭaphalasiddhyai cetyatraivedamabhāṣata /
sāñjanā api ye mantrā gāruḍādyā na te param // 137
15.d:
यथेष्टफलसिद्ध्यै चेत्यत्रैवेदमभाषत ।
साञ्जना अपि ये मन्त्रा गारुडाद्या न ते परम् ॥ 137
15.m:
'and for the attainment of any desired result'; in this very text it was declared:
Even mantras that possess residual traces, such as the Gāruḍa mantras, not only // 137

15.s:
mālinyā pūritāḥ sidhdyai balādeva tu muktaye /
tasmātphalepsurapyanya mantraṃ nyasyātra mālinīm // 138
15.d:
मालिन्या पूरिताः सिध्द्यै बलादेव तु मुक्तये ।
तस्मात्फलेप्सुरप्यन्य मन्त्रं न्यस्यात्र मालिनीम् ॥ 138
15.m:
are brought to completion by Mālinī for accomplishment, but inevitably for liberation as well.
Therefore, even one desiring [worldly] fruits, having imposed another mantra, should impose Mālinī here, // 138

15.s:
nyasyejjaptvāpica japedayatnādapavṛktaye /
ityevaṃ mātṛkāṃ nyasyenmālinīṃ vā kramāddvayam // 139
15.d:
न्यस्येज्जप्त्वापिच जपेदयत्नादपवृक्तये ।
इत्येवं मातृकां न्यस्येन्मालिनीं वा क्रमाद्द्वयम् ॥ 139
15.m:
and having recited it, should also recite [Mālinī], for effortless liberation.
Thus one should impose Mātṛkā or Mālinī, or both in succession, // 139

15.s:
siddhimuktyanusārādvā varṇānvā yugapaddvayoḥ /
akṣahrīṃ naphahrīmetau piṇḍau saṃghāvihānayoḥ // 140
15.d:
सिद्धिमुक्त्यनुसाराद्वा वर्णान्वा युगपद्द्वयोः ।
अक्षह्रीं नफह्रीमेतौ पिण्डौ संघाविहानयोः ॥ 140
15.m:
according to whether one pursues accomplishment or liberation, or the letters of both simultaneously.
'Akṣahrīṃ' and 'naphahrīṃ': these two are the conglomerate aggregates // 140

15.s:
vācakau nyāsa etābhyāṃ kṛte nyāse'thavaikakaḥ /
eṣa cāṅgatanubrahmayukto vā tadviparyayaḥ // 141
15.d:
वाचकौ न्यास एताभ्यां कृते न्यासेऽथवैककः ।
एष चाङ्गतनुब्रह्मयुक्तो वा तद्विपर्ययः ॥ 141
15.m:
designating these two here. Imposition is performed by these two, or singly.
And this [imposition] may be accompanied by limbs, bodily mantras, and Brahmans, or the reverse. // 141

15.s:
sāmudāyikavinyāse pṛthak piṇḍāvimau kramāt /
akramādathavā nyasyedekamevātha yojayet // 142
15.d:
सामुदायिकविन्यासे पृथक् पिण्डाविमौ क्रमात् ।
अक्रमादथवा न्यस्येदेकमेवाथ योजयेत् ॥ 142
15.m:
In the collective imposition, one should impose these two aggregates separately in succession,
or without succession, or combine them into one. // 142

15.s:
kriyayā siddhikāmo yaḥ sa kriyāṃ bhūyasīṃ caret /
anīpsurapi yastasmai bhūyase svaphalāya sā // 143
15.d:
क्रियया सिद्धिकामो यः स क्रियां भूयसीं चरेत् ।
अनीप्सुरपि यस्तस्मै भूयसे स्वफलाय सा ॥ 143
15.m:
He who desires accomplishment through action should perform extensive action;
even for one who does not desire it, it leads to its own greater fruit. // 143

15.s:
yastu dhyānajapābhyāsaiḥ siddhīpsuḥ sa kriyāṃ param /
saṃskṛtyai svecchayā kuryāt prāṅnayenātha bhūyasīm // 144
15.d:
यस्तु ध्यानजपाभ्यासैः सिद्धीप्सुः स क्रियां परम् ।
संस्कृत्यै स्वेच्छया कुर्यात् प्राङ्नयेनाथ भूयसीम् ॥ 144
15.m:
Whereas he who desires accomplishment through the practice of meditation and recitation should perform extensive action
only for purification according to his wish, in accordance with the previously explained principle. // 144

15.s:
mumukṣuratha tasmai vā yathābhīṣṭaṃ samācaret /
śivatāpattirevārtho hyeṣāṃ nyāsādikarmaṇām // 145
15.d:
मुमुक्षुरथ तस्मै वा यथाभीष्टं समाचरेत् ।
शिवतापत्तिरेवार्थो ह्येषां न्यासादिकर्मणाम् ॥ 145
15.m:
Or for the seeker of liberation, one should perform [action] according to his wish;
for the attainment of Śivahood is indeed the purpose of these rites such as imposition. // 145

15.s:
evaṃ nyāsaṃ vidhāyārghapātre vidhimupācaret /
uktanītyaiva tatpaścāt pūjayennyastavācakaiḥ // 146
15.d:
एवं न्यासं विधायार्घपात्रे विधिमुपाचरेत् ।
उक्तनीत्यैव तत्पश्चात् पूजयेन्न्यस्तवाचकैः ॥ 146
15.m:
Having thus performed the imposition, one should carry out the rite on the vessel of respectful offering;
following the stated method, one should thereafter worship using the designators that have been imposed. // 146

15.s:
yataḥ samastabhāvānāṃ śivātsiddhimayādatho /
pūrṇādavyatirekitvaṃ kārakāṇāmihārcayā // 147
15.d:
यतः समस्तभावानां शिवात्सिद्धिमयादथो ।
पूर्णादव्यतिरेकित्वं कारकाणामिहार्चया ॥ 147
15.m:
Since all entities are non-different from Śiva, who consists of accomplishment,
and from fullness, here through worship the case-factors // 147

15.s:
samastaṃ kārakavrātaṃ śivābhinnaṃ pradarśitam /
pūjodāharaṇe sarvaṃ vyaśnute gamanādyapi // 148
15.d:
समस्तं कारकव्रातं शिवाभिन्नं प्रदर्शितम् ।
पूजोदाहरणे सर्वं व्यश्नुते गमनाद्यपि ॥ 148
15.m:
— the entire host of case-factors — are shown to be non-different from Śiva.
In the example of worship, this pervades everything, even walking and the like. // 148

15.s:
yathāhi vāhakaṭakabhramasvātantryamāgataḥ /
aśvaḥ saṃgrāmarūḍho'pi tāṃ śikṣāṃ nātivartate // 149
15.d:
यथाहि वाहकटकभ्रमस्वातन्त्र्यमागतः ।
अश्वः संग्रामरूढोऽपि तां शिक्षां नातिवर्तते ॥ 149
15.m:
Just as a horse, having attained freedom in the turns and circles directed by its rider,
even when entered into battle does not transgress that training, // 149

15.s:
tathārcanakriyābhyāsaśivībhāvitakārakaḥ /
gacchaṃstiṣṭhannapi dvaitaṃ kārakāṇāṃ vyapojjhati // 150
15.d:
तथार्चनक्रियाभ्यासशिवीभावितकारकः ।
गच्छंस्तिष्ठन्नपि द्वैतं कारकाणां व्यपोज्झति ॥ 150
15.m:
so one whose case-factors are made identical with Śiva by the practice of the rite of worship,
even while walking or standing, casts away the duality of case-factors. // 150

15.s:
tathaikyābhyāsaniṣṭhasyākramādviśvamidaṃ haṭhāt /
saṃpūrṇaśivatākṣobhanarīnartadiva sphuret // 151
15.d:
तथैक्याभ्यासनिष्ठस्याक्रमाद्विश्वमिदं हठात् ।
संपूर्णशिवताक्षोभनरीनर्तदिव स्फुरेत् ॥ 151
15.m:
Likewise, for one established in the practice of unity, this entire universe flashes forth,
suddenly and without succession, as if dancing with the agitation of full Śivahood. // 151

15.s:
uvāca pūjanastotre hyasmākaṃ paramo guruḥ /
aho svādurasaḥ ko'pi śivapūjāmayotsavaḥ // 152
15.d:
उवाच पूजनस्तोत्रे ह्यस्माकं परमो गुरुः ।
अहो स्वादुरसः कोऽपि शिवपूजामयोत्सवः ॥ 152
15.m:
For our supreme guru said in the Pūjanastotra:
'Ah, of what indescribable sweet savor is this festival consisting of the worship of Śiva, // 152

15.s:
ṣaṭtriṃśato'pi tattvānāṃ kṣobho yatrollasatyalam /
tadetādṛkpūrṇaśivaviśvāveśāya ye'rcanam // 153
15.d:
षट्त्रिंशतोऽपि तत्त्वानां क्षोभो यत्रोल्लसत्यलम् ।
तदेतादृक्पूर्णशिवविश्वावेशाय येऽर्चनम् ॥ 153
15.m:
wherein the agitation of even the thirty-six principles bursts forth completely!'
Therefore, those who perform worship for the sake of entering into such a full, Śiva-like universe, // 153

15.s:
kurvanti te śivā eva tānpūrṇānprati kiṃ phalam /
vināpi jñānayogābhyāṃ kriyā nyāsārcanādikā // 154
15.d:
कुर्वन्ति ते शिवा एव तान्पूर्णान्प्रति किं फलम् ।
विनापि ज्ञानयोगाभ्यां क्रिया न्यासार्चनादिका ॥ 154
15.m:
are Śiva himself; for those who are full, what fruit could there be?
Even without knowledge and yoga, action such as imposition and worship, // 154

15.s:
itthamaikyasamāpattidānātparaphalapradā /
sādhakasyāpi tatsadvipradamantraikatāṃ gatam // 155
15.d:
इत्थमैक्यसमापत्तिदानात्परफलप्रदा ।
साधकस्यापि तत्सद्विप्रदमन्त्रैकतां गतम् ॥ 155
15.m:
bestowing the highest fruit in this manner by granting absorption in unity,
leads the universe — which has attained unity with the mantra that grants true accomplishment — // 155

15.s:
viśvaṃ vrajadavighnatvaṃ svāṃ siddhiṃ śīghramāvahet /
uktaṃ ca parameśena na vidhirnārcanakramaḥ // 156
15.d:
विश्वं व्रजदविघ्नत्वं स्वां सिद्धिं शीघ्रमावहेत् ।
उक्तं च परमेशेन न विधिर्नार्चनक्रमः ॥ 156
15.m:
to freedom from obstacles, and quickly brings its own accomplishment to the adept.
And it was said by the Supreme Lord: 'There is no rule and no sequence of worship; // 156

15.s:
kevalaṃ smaraṇātsiddhirvāñchiteti matādiṣu /
tadevaṃ tanmayībhāvadāyinyarcākriyā yataḥ // 157
15.d:
केवलं स्मरणात्सिद्धिर्वाञ्छितेति मतादिषु ।
तदेवं तन्मयीभावदायिन्यर्चाक्रिया यतः ॥ 157
15.m:
the desired accomplishment comes merely from remembrance' in teachings such as the Mata.
Therefore, since the rite of worship thus grants identification with that, // 157

15.s:
samastakārakaikātmyaṃ tenāsyāḥ paramaṃ vapuḥ /
yaṣṭrādhārasya tādātmyaṃ sthānaśuddhividhikramāt // 158
15.d:
समस्तकारकैकात्म्यं तेनास्याः परमं वपुः ।
यष्ट्राधारस्य तादात्म्यं स्थानशुद्धिविधिक्रमात् ॥ 158
15.m:
the identity of all case-factors is its supreme form.
The identity of the worshiper and the substrate [arises] through the procedure of site purification; // 158

15.s:
yaṣṭṛyājyatadādhārakaraṇādānasaṃpradāḥ /
nyāsakrameṇa śivatātādātmyamadhiśerate // 159
15.d:
यष्टृयाज्यतदाधारकरणादानसंप्रदाः ।
न्यासक्रमेण शिवतातादात्म्यमधिशेरते ॥ 159
15.m:
the worshiper, the offering, its substrate, the instrument, the ablative source, and the recipient
repose in identity with Śivahood through the sequence of imposition. // 159

15.s:
arghapātramapādānaṃ tasmādādīyate yataḥ /
yacca tatsthaṃ jalādyetatkaraṇaṃ śodhane'rcane // 160
15.d:
अर्घपात्रमपादानं तस्मादादीयते यतः ।
यच्च तत्स्थं जलाद्येतत्करणं शोधनेऽर्चने ॥ 160
15.m:
The offering vessel is the source, since it is taken from it;
and the water and other ingredients situated therein are the instrument in purification and worship. // 160

15.s:
arghapātrāmbuvipruḍbhiḥ spṛṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ hi śudhyati /
śivārkakarasaṃsparśātkānyā śuddhirbhaviṣyati // 161
15.d:
अर्घपात्राम्बुविप्रुड्भिः स्पृष्टं सर्वं हि शुध्यति ।
शिवार्ककरसंस्पर्शात्कान्या शुद्धिर्भविष्यति ॥ 161
15.m:
Everything touched by drops of water from the offering vessel is indeed purified;
from the touch of the rays of the sun of Śiva, what other purification could there be? // 161

15.s:
ūce śrīpūrvaśāstre tadarghapātravidhau vibhuḥ /
na cāsaṃśodhitaṃ vastu kiṃcidapyupakalpayet // 162
15.d:
ऊचे श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे तदर्घपात्रविधौ विभुः ।
न चासंशोधितं वस्तु किंचिदप्युपकल्पयेत् ॥ 162
15.m:
The all-pervading Lord spoke thus in the venerable Pūrvaśāstra regarding the rule of the offering vessel:
'And one must not offer any unpurified substance whatsoever.' // 162

15.s:
tena śuddhaṃ tu sarvaṃ yadaśuddhamapi tacchuci /
aśuddhatā ca vijñeyā paśutacchāsanāśayāt // 163
15.d:
तेन शुद्धं तु सर्वं यदशुद्धमपि तच्छुचि ।
अशुद्धता च विज्ञेया पशुतच्छासनाशयात् ॥ 163
15.m:
Therefore whatever is purified is pure, and even what is impure is pure.
Impurity is to be understood as arising from the mindset of bound souls and their scriptures, // 163

15.s:
svatādavasthyātpūrvasmādathavāpyupakalpitāt /
tena yadyadihāsannaṃ saṃvidaścidanugrahāt // 164
15.d:
स्वतादवस्थ्यात्पूर्वस्मादथवाप्युपकल्पितात् ।
तेन यद्यदिहासन्नं संविदश्चिदनुग्रहात् ॥ 164
15.m:
or from its previous natural condition, or even from conceptual projection.
Therefore, whatever in this world is proximate to consciousness through the grace of consciousness, // 164

15.s:
kiyato'pi tadatyantaṃ yogyaṃ yāge'tra jīvavat /
anena nayayogena yadāsattividūrate // 165
15.d:
कियतोऽपि तदत्यन्तं योग्यं यागेऽत्र जीववत् ।
अनेन नययोगेन यदासत्तिविदूरते ॥ 165
15.m:
to whatever extent, is entirely suitable for this sacrifice, like a living being.
By applying this principle, according to the proximity or distance // 165

15.s:
saṃvideti tadā tatra yogyāyogyatvamādiśet /
vīrāṇāmata eveha mithaḥ svapratimāmṛtam // 166
15.d:
संविदेति तदा तत्र योग्यायोग्यत्वमादिशेत् ।
वीराणामत एवेह मिथः स्वप्रतिमामृतम् ॥ 166
15.m:
of consciousness, one should determine suitability and unsuitability therein.
For this very reason, the mutually produced nectar reflecting themselves // 166

15.s:
tattadyāgavidhāviṣṭaṃ gurubhirbhāvitātmabhiḥ /
unmajjayati nirmagnāṃ saṃvidaṃ yattu suṣṭhu tat // 167
15.d:
तत्तद्यागविधाविष्टं गुरुभिर्भावितात्मभिः ।
उन्मज्जयति निर्मग्नां संविदं यत्तु सुष्ठु तत् ॥ 167
15.m:
is prescribed for heroes in the ritual of various sacrifices by the gurus who have cultivated their self.
That which thoroughly raises submerged consciousness // 167

15.s:
arcāyai yogyamānando yasmādunmagnatā citaḥ /
tenācidrūpadehādiprādhānyavinimajjakam // 168
15.d:
अर्चायै योग्यमानन्दो यस्मादुन्मग्नता चितः ।
तेनाचिद्रूपदेहादिप्राधान्यविनिमज्जकम् ॥ 168
15.m:
is suitable for worship, because bliss is the emergence of consciousness.
Therefore, whatever submerges the primacy of unconscious forms such as the body, // 168

15.s:
ānandajananaṃ pūjāyogyaṃ hṛdayahāri yat /
ataḥ kulakramottīrṇatrikasāramatādiṣu // 169
15.d:
आनन्दजननं पूजायोग्यं हृदयहारि यत् ।
अतः कुलक्रमोत्तीर्णत्रिकसारमतादिषु ॥ 169
15.m:
generates bliss, and captivates the heart is suitable for worship.
Hence in doctrines such as the Trikasāra, which transcends the Kula tradition, // 169

15.s:
madyakādambarīśīdhudravyādermahimā param /
lokasthitiṃ racayituṃ madyādeḥ paśuśāsane // 170
15.d:
मद्यकादम्बरीशीधुद्रव्यादेर्महिमा परम् ।
लोकस्थितिं रचयितुं मद्यादेः पशुशासने ॥ 170
15.m: The supremacy of substances such as wine, kādambarī, and śīdhu is ultimate [in our systems]; / however, in the teaching for bound souls, impurity is proclaimed regarding wine and the like, in order to maintain worldly order. // 170

15.s:
proktā hyaśuddhistatraiva tasya kvāpi viśuddhatā /
pañcagavye pavitratvaṃ somacarṇanapātrayoḥ // 171
15.d:
प्रोक्ता ह्यशुद्धिस्तत्रैव तस्य क्वापि विशुद्धता ।
पञ्चगव्ये पवित्रत्वं सोमचर्णनपात्रयोः ॥ 171
15.m: Yet even there, in certain contexts, its purity is stated: / [such as] the purifying nature of the five bovine products, and the rule regarding the Soma and caru vessels, // 171

15.s:
vidhiścāvabhṛthasnānaṃ haste kṛṣṇaviṣāṇitā /
na patnyā ca vinā yāgaḥ sarvadaivatatulyatā // 172
15.d:
विधिश्चावभृथस्नानं हस्ते कृष्णविषाणिता ।
न पत्न्या च विना यागः सर्वदैवततुल्यता ॥ 172
15.m: the ritual ablution at the conclusion of sacrifice, holding the blackbuck horn in one's hand, / no sacrifice [being performed] without a wife, and equality with all deities, // 172

15.s:
surāhutirbrahmasatre vapāntrahṛdayāhutiḥ /
pāśaveṣvapi śāstreṣu tadadarśi maheśinā // 173
15.d:
सुराहुतिर्ब्रह्मसत्रे वपान्त्रहृदयाहुतिः ।
पाशवेष्वपि शास्त्रेषु तददर्शि महेशिना ॥ 173
15.m: the oblation of wine in the Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice, and the offering of the omentum, entrails, and heart [in animal sacrifices]. / Even in the scriptures for bound souls, that was revealed by the Great Lord // 173

15.s:
ghorāndhyahaimananiśāmadhyagāciradīptivat /
bhakṣyo haṃso na bhakṣyo'sāviti ripratipattiṣu // 174
15.d:
घोरान्ध्यहैमननिशामध्यगाचिरदीप्तिवत् ।
भक्ष्यो हंसो न भक्ष्योऽसाविति रिप्रतिपत्तिषु ॥ 174
15.m: like a sudden flash of lightning in the midst of a dreadfully dark winter night. / Amid conflicting claims in the Smṛti traditions— / as to whether 'the swan is edible' or 'it is not edible'— // 174

15.s:
smārtīṣu vijayatyeko yaḥ śivābhedaśuddhikaḥ /
ajñatvavedādarśitvarāgadveṣādayo hyamī // 175
15.d:
स्मार्तीषु विजयत्येको यः शिवाभेदशुद्धिकः ।
अज्ञत्ववेदादर्शित्वरागद्वेषादयो ह्यमी ॥ 175
15.m: that sole [standard] triumphs whose purity consists in non-duality with Śiva. / For such [flaws] as ignorance, lack of Vedic vision, attachment, and aversion // 175

15.s:
munīnāṃ vacasi svasminprāmāṇyonmūlanakṣamāḥ /
vede'pi yadabhakṣyaṃ tadbhakṣyamityupadiśyate // 176
15.d:
मुनीनां वचसि स्वस्मिन्प्रामाण्योन्मूलनक्षमाः ।
वेदेऽपि यदभक्ष्यं तद्भक्ष्यमित्युपदिश्यते ॥ 176
15.m: are capable of eradicating authority from the sages' own words. / Even in the Veda, that which is inedible is taught to be edible [in specific rituals]; // 176

15.s:
na vidhipratiṣedhākhyadharmayorekamāspadam /
atha tatra na tadbhakṣyaṃ tadā tena tathā tataḥ // 177
15.d:
न विधिप्रतिषेधाख्यधर्मयोरेकमास्पदम् ।
अथ तत्र न तद्भक्ष्यं तदा तेन तथा ततः ॥ 177
15.m: for the two properties called injunction and prohibition cannot share a single scope. / If you say that there it is not [ordinarily] edible, then precisely because of that [qualification, it is so]. // 177

15.s:
evaṃ viṣayabhedānno śivokterbādhikā śrutiḥ /
kvacidviṣayatulyatvādbādhyabādhakatā yadi // 178
15.d:
एवं विषयभेदान्नो शिवोक्तेर्बाधिका श्रुतिः ।
क्वचिद्विषयतुल्यत्वाद्बाध्यबाधकता यदि ॥ 178
15.m: Thus, due to the difference in scope, Vedic revelation does not invalidate the utterance of Śiva. / If anywhere there were invalidation because the scope is identical, // 178

15.s:
tadbādhyā śrutireveti prāgevaitannirūpitam /
prakṛtaṃ brūmahe kṛtvā nyāsaṃ dehārghapātrayoḥ // 179
15.d:
तद्बाध्या श्रुतिरेवेति प्रागेवैतन्निरूपितम् ।
प्रकृतं ब्रूमहे कृत्वा न्यासं देहार्घपात्रयोः ॥ 179
15.m: then it is Vedic revelation itself that is invalidated; this has already been established before. / We now state the topic at hand: having performed the imposition on the body and the offering vessel, // 179

15.s:
sāmānyamarghapātrāmbhovipruḍbhiḥ prokṣya cākhilam /
yāgopakaraṇaṃ paścādbāhyayāgaṃ samācaret // 180
15.d:
सामान्यमर्घपात्राम्भोविप्रुड्भिः प्रोक्ष्य चाखिलम् ।
यागोपकरणं पश्चाद्बाह्ययागं समाचरेत् ॥ 180
15.m: and having sprinkled all the sacrificial implements generally with drops of water from the offering vessel, / one should then perform the external sacrifice. // 180

15.s:
prabhāmaṇḍalake khe vā suliptāyāṃ ca vā bhuvi /
triśūlārkavṛṣāndikasthā mātaraḥ kṣetrapaṃ yajet // 181
15.d:
प्रभामण्डलके खे वा सुलिप्तायां च वा भुवि ।
त्रिशूलार्कवृषान्दिकस्था मातरः क्षेत्रपं यजेत् ॥ 181
15.m: In a radiant diagram, in the ether, or on well-smeared ground, / one should worship the Mothers stationed at the trident, sun, bull, and other [positions], and the Protector of the Field, // 181

15.s:
yoginīśca pṛthaṅmantrairoṃnamonāmayojitaiḥ /
ekoccāreṇa vā bāhyaparivāretiśabditāḥ // 182
15.d:
योगिनीश्च पृथङ्मन्त्रैरोंनमोनामयोजितैः ।
एकोच्चारेण वा बाह्यपरिवारेतिशब्दिताः ॥ 182
15.m: as well as the Yoginīs, either with individual mantras joined with Oṃ, namaḥ, and [their] name, / or with a single recitation, designated as the 'outer retinue.' // 182

15.s:
tāro nāma caturthyantaṃ namaścetyarcane manuḥ /
evaṃ bahiḥ pūjayitvā dvāraṃ prokṣya prapūjayet // 183
15.d:
तारो नाम चतुर्थ्यन्तं नमश्चेत्यर्चने मनुः ।
एवं बहिः पूजयित्वा द्वारं प्रोक्ष्य प्रपूजयेत् ॥ 183
15.m: The mantra in worship consists of the praṇava, the name ending in the dative case, and 'namaḥ'. / Having thus worshipped outside, one should sprinkle the doorway and worship [it]. // 183

15.s:
triśiraḥśāsanādau ca sa dṛṣṭo vidhirucyate /
gaṇeśalakṣmyau dvārordhve dakṣe vāme tayoḥ punaḥ // 184
15.d:
त्रिशिरःशासनादौ च स दृष्टो विधिरुच्यते ।
गणेशलक्ष्म्यौ द्वारोर्ध्वे दक्षे वामे तयोः पुनः ॥ 184
15.m: That rite which is observed in the Triśiraḥśāsana and other texts is now stated: / Gaṇeśa and Lakṣmī are above the door, to the right and left; between them, // 184

15.s:
madhye vāgīśvarīṃ diṇḍimahodarayugaṃ tathā /
kramātsvadakṣavāmasthaṃ tathaitena krameṇa ca // 185
15.d:
मध्ये वागीश्वरीं दिण्डिमहोदरयुगं तथा ।
क्रमात्स्वदक्षवामस्थं तथैतेन क्रमेण च ॥ 185
15.m: in the middle, [one should worship] Vāgīśvarī, and likewise the pair Diṇḍi and Mahodara / stationed respectively to one's own right and left; and in this sequence, // 185

15.s:
ekaikaṃ pūjayetsamyaṅ nandikālau trimārgagām /
kālindīṃ chāgameṣāsyau svadakṣāddvāḥsthaśākhayoḥ // 186
15.d:
एकैकं पूजयेत्सम्यङ् नन्दिकालौ त्रिमार्गगाम् ।
कालिन्दीं छागमेषास्यौ स्वदक्षाद्द्वाःस्थशाखयोः ॥ 186
15.m: one should properly worship each one: Nandin and Kāla; the Ganges flowing through the three worlds / and the Yamunā; the goat-faced and the ram-faced [attendants] on the doorposts starting from one's right; // 186

15.s:
adhodehalyananteśādhāraśaktīśca pūjayet /
dvāramadhye sarasvatyā mahāstraṃ pūjayedamī // 187
15.d:
अधोदेहल्यनन्तेशाधारशक्तीश्च पूजयेत् ।
द्वारमध्ये सरस्वत्या महास्त्रं पूजयेदमी ॥ 187
15.m: and beneath the threshold, one should worship Ananteśa and the Supporting Powers; / in the middle of the door, [along] with Sarasvatī, one should worship the great weapon. All these // 187

15.s:
padmādhāragatāḥ sarve'pyuditā vighnanāśakāḥ /
pūjane pūrvavanmantro dīpakadvayakalpitaḥ // 188
15.d:
पद्माधारगताः सर्वेऽप्युदिता विघ्ननाशकाः ।
पूजने पूर्ववन्मन्त्रो दीपकद्वयकल्पितः ॥ 188
15.m: are seated upon a lotus base and are proclaimed as destroyers of obstacles. / In the worship, the mantra is as before, formulated with two illuminating words [Oṃ and namaḥ]. // 188

15.s:
arghapuṣpasamālambhadhūpanaivedyavandanaiḥ /
pūjāṃ kuryādihārghaścāpyuttamadravyayojitaḥ // 189
15.d:
अर्घपुष्पसमालम्भधूपनैवेद्यवन्दनैः ।
पूजां कुर्यादिहार्घश्चाप्युत्तमद्रव्ययोजितः ॥ 189
15.m: One should perform worship with guest-water, flowers, fragrant pastes, incense, food offerings, and prostrations; / and here the guest-water is also prepared with the highest substance [wine]. // 189

15.s:
ekoccāreṇa vā kuryāddvāḥsthadaivatapūjanam /
rahasyapūjāṃ cetkuryāttadbāhyaparivārakam // 190
15.d:
एकोच्चारेण वा कुर्याद्द्वाःस्थदैवतपूजनम् ।
रहस्यपूजां चेत्कुर्यात्तद्बाह्यपरिवारकम् ॥ 190
15.m: Or one may perform the worship of the deities situated at the door with a single recitation. / If one performs the esoteric worship, then [one should worship] the outer retinue // 190

15.s:
dvāḥsthāṃśca pūjayedantardevāgre kalpanākramāt /
kṣiptvāstrajaptaṃ kusumaṃ jvaladveśmani vghnanut // 191
15.d:
द्वाःस्थांश्च पूजयेदन्तर्देवाग्रे कल्पनाक्रमात् ।
क्षिप्त्वास्त्रजप्तं कुसुमं ज्वलद्वेश्मनि व्घ्ननुत् ॥ 191
15.m: and the door-keepers internally before the deity according to the order of visualization. / Having cast a flower consecrated with the weapon-mantra into the blazing chamber, dispelling obstacles, // 191

15.s:
praviśya śivaraśmīddhadṛśā veśmāvalokayet /
diśo'streṇa ca badhnīyācchādayedvarmaṇākhilāḥ // 192
15.d:
प्रविश्य शिवरश्मीद्धदृशा वेश्मावलोकयेत् ।
दिशोऽस्त्रेण च बध्नीयाच्छादयेद्वर्मणाखिलाः ॥ 192
15.m: and having entered, one should gaze upon the chamber with a vision kindled by the rays of Śiva; / one should bind the directions with the weapon-mantra and cover them all with the armor-mantra. // 192

15.s:
tatrottarāśābhimukho mumukṣustādṛśāya vā /
viśettathā hyaghorāgniḥ pāśānpluṣyati bandhakān // 193
15.d:
तत्रोत्तराशाभिमुखो मुमुक्षुस्तादृशाय वा ।
विशेत्तथा ह्यघोराग्निः पाशान्प्लुष्यति बन्धकान् ॥ 193
15.m: One who desires liberation, or [acts] for one of that kind, should enter there facing the northern direction; / for in this way the Aghora-fire incinerates the binding fetters. // 193

15.s:
yadyapyasti na diṅnāma kācitpūrvāparādikā /
pratyayo hi na tasyāḥ syādekasyā anupāhiteḥ // 194
15.d:
यद्यप्यस्ति न दिङ्नाम काचित्पूर्वापरादिका ।
प्रत्ययो हि न तस्याः स्यादेकस्या अनुपाहितेः ॥ 194
15.m: Even though, in truth, no direction such as 'east' or 'west' exists, / for there could be no perception of an unconditioned single [space], // 194

15.s:
upādhiḥ pūrvatādiṣṭa iti cettatkṛtaṃ diśā /
upādhimātraṃ tu tathā vaicitryāya kathaṃ bhavet // 195
15.d:
उपाधिः पूर्वतादिष्ट इति चेत्तत्कृतं दिशा ।
उपाधिमात्रं तु तथा वैचित्र्याय कथं भवेत् ॥ 195
15.m: if it is argued that an extrinsic delimiter like 'easternness' is posited, what is accomplished by the direction itself? / Nor could a mere extrinsic delimiter account for such manifold variety. // 195

15.s:
tasmātsaṃvitprakāśo'yaṃ mūrtyābhāsanabhāgataḥ /
pūrvādidigvibhāgākhyavaicitryollekhadurmadaḥ // 196
15.d:
तस्मात्संवित्प्रकाशोऽयं मूर्त्याभासनभागतः ।
पूर्वादिदिग्विभागाख्यवैचित्र्योल्लेखदुर्मदः ॥ 196
15.m: Therefore, it is this very luminosity of consciousness that, through its role in manifesting forms, / revels in the manifestation of diversity called the division of directions such as east. // 196

15.s:
tatra yadyatprakāśena sadā svīkaraṇe kṣamam /
tadevordhvaṃ prakāśātma sparśāyogyamadhaḥ punaḥ // 197
15.d:
तत्र यद्यत्प्रकाशेन सदा स्वीकरणे क्षमम् ।
तदेवोर्ध्वं प्रकाशात्म स्पर्शायोग्यमधः पुनः ॥ 197
15.m: Therein, whatever is ever capable of being appropriated by luminosity / is the zenith, whose nature is luminosity; and what is unfit for contact is the nadir. // 197

15.s:
kiṃcitprakāśatā madhyaṃ tato vai diksamudbhavaḥ /
kiṃcitprakāśayogyasya saṃmukhaṃ prasaratpuraḥ // 198
15.d:
किंचित्प्रकाशता मध्यं ततो वै दिक्समुद्भवः ।
किंचित्प्रकाशयोग्यस्य संमुखं प्रसरत्पुरः ॥ 198
15.m: The middle is partial luminosity; from that indeed arises the directions. / What extends forward directly facing that which is fit for partial luminosity is the front [the east]; // 198

15.s:
parāṅmukhaṃ tu tatpaścāditi digdvayamāgatam /
prakāśaḥ saṃmukhaṃ vastu gṛhītvodriktaraśmikaḥ // 199
15.d:
पराङ्मुखं तु तत्पश्चादिति दिग्द्वयमागतम् ।
प्रकाशः संमुखं वस्तु गृहीत्वोद्रिक्तरश्मिकः ॥ 199
15.m: and what faces away from it is the back [the west]—thus a pair of directions arises. / Luminosity, having seized an object directly in front, with its rays surging forth, // 199

15.s:
yatra tiṣṭhoddakṣiṇaṃ tatprakāśasyānukūlyataḥ /
dakṣiṇasya puraḥsaṃsthaṃ vāmamityupadiśyate // 200
15.d:
यत्र तिष्ठोद्दक्षिणं तत्प्रकाशस्यानुकूल्यतः ।
दक्षिणस्य पुरःसंस्थं वाममित्युपदिश्यते ॥ 200
15.m: where it abides, that is the right [the south], owing to its conformity with luminosity; / what stands in front of the right is taught as the left [the north]. // 200

15.s:
tatprakāśitameyendusparśasaumyaṃ tadeva hi /
evamāśācatuṣke'sminmadhyaviśrāntiyogataḥ // 201
15.d:
तत्प्रकाशितमेयेन्दुस्पर्शसौम्यं तदेव हि ।
एवमाशाचतुष्केऽस्मिन्मध्यविश्रान्तियोगतः ॥ 201
15.m: That indeed is gentle through contact with the moon of the knowable illuminated by it. / In this quartet of directions, through the junction of resting in the intermediate spaces, // 201

15.s:
catuṣkamanyattenāṣṭau diśastattadadhiṣṭhitāḥ /
evaṃ prakāśamātre'sminvarade parame śive // 202
15.d:
चतुष्कमन्यत्तेनाष्टौ दिशस्तत्तदधिष्ठिताः ।
एवं प्रकाशमात्रेऽस्मिन्वरदे परमे शिवे ॥ 202
15.m: another quartet [arises]; thereby there are eight directions presided over by their respective deities. / Thus, within this pure luminosity, the boon-bestowing Supreme Śiva, // 202

15.s:
digvibhāgaḥ sthito loke śāstre'pica tathocyate /
kramātsadāśivādhīśaḥ pañcamantratanuryataḥ // 203
15.d:
दिग्विभागः स्थितो लोके शास्त्रेऽपिच तथोच्यते ।
क्रमात्सदाशिवाधीशः पञ्चमन्त्रतनुर्यतः ॥ 203
15.m: the division of directions is situated in the world, and it is also spoken of thus in scripture. / Because Sadāśiva, the sovereign whose body consists of the five mantras, // 203

15.s:
īśanraghoravāmākhyasadyo'dhobhedato diśaḥ /
īśa ūrdhvaṃ prakāśatvātpūrvaṃ vaktraṃ prasāri yat // 204
15.d:
ईशन्रघोरवामाख्यसद्योऽधोभेदतो दिशः ।
ईश ऊर्ध्वं प्रकाशत्वात्पूर्वं वक्त्रं प्रसारि यत् ॥ 204
15.m: divides the directions through the distinctions of Īśāna, Tatpuruṣa, Aghora, Vāmadeva, and Sadyojāta, / Īśāna is the zenith because of its luminous nature; the face that extends forward is the east; // 204

15.s:
puruṣo dakṣiṇācaṇḍo vāmā vāmastu saumyakaḥ /
parāṅmukhatayā sadyaḥ paścimā paribhāṣyate // 205
15.d:
पुरुषो दक्षिणाचण्डो वामा वामस्तु सौम्यकः ।
पराङ्मुखतया सद्यः पश्चिमा परिभाष्यते ॥ 205
15.m: Puruṣa is the south, fierce; Vāmā [is the north], gentle because it is on the left; / because it turns away, Sadyojāta is defined as the west; // 205

15.s:
pātālavaktramadharamaprakāśatayā sthiteḥ /
khamarudvahnijalabhūkhāni vaktrāṇyamuṣya hi // 206
15.d:
पातालवक्त्रमधरमप्रकाशतया स्थितेः ।
खमरुद्वह्निजलभूखानि वक्त्राण्यमुष्य हि ॥ 206
15.m: the subterranean face is the lowest, because it abides in non-luminosity. / Indeed, space, wind, fire, water, and earth are his faces. // 206

15.s:
mukhyatvena khamevordhvaṃ prakāśamayamucyate /
tadeva mukhyato'dhastādaprakāśaṃ yataḥ sphuṭam // 207
15.d:
मुख्यत्वेन खमेवोर्ध्वं प्रकाशमयमुच्यते ।
तदेव मुख्यतोऽधस्तादप्रकाशं यतः स्फुटम् ॥ 207
15.m: Primarily, space alone is said to be upward, consisting of luminosity; / that very [element], primarily below, is clearly non-luminous. // 207

15.s:
madhye tu yatprakāśaṃ tanna prakāśyaṃ na cetarat /
prakāśatvāddiśyamānamato'smindikcatuṣṭayam // 208
15.d:
मध्ये तु यत्प्रकाशं तन्न प्रकाश्यं न चेतरत् ।
प्रकाशत्वाद्दिश्यमानमतोऽस्मिन्दिक्चतुष्टयम् ॥ 208
15.m: In the middle, that which is luminosity is neither merely to be illuminated nor something other; / because it is luminosity, it is being pointed out; therefore, within it is the quartet of directions. // 208

15.s:
pañcamantratanurnātha itthaṃ viśvadigīśvaraḥ /
tato'pīśastathā rudro viṣṇurbrahmā tathā sthitaḥ // 209
15.d:
पञ्चमन्त्रतनुर्नाथ इत्थं विश्वदिगीश्वरः ।
ततोऽपीशस्तथा रुद्रो विष्णुर्ब्रह्मा तथा स्थितः ॥ 209
15.m: The Lord whose body consists of the five mantras is thus the sovereign of all directions. / From him, likewise, abide Īśa, Rudra, Viṣṇu, and Brahmā. // 209

15.s:
ūrdhvābhivyaktyayogyatvādviṣṇordhātuśca pañcamam /
na vaktraṃ tau bhedamayau sṛṣṭisthitiprabhū yataḥ // 210
15.d:
ऊर्ध्वाभिव्यक्त्ययोग्यत्वाद्विष्णोर्धातुश्च पञ्चमम् ।
न वक्त्रं तौ भेदमयौ सृष्टिस्थितिप्रभू यतः ॥ 210
15.m: Because they are incapable of expressing the upward direction, Viṣṇu and the Creator do not have a fifth / face, since they consist of differentiation, being the lords of emission and stasis. // 210

15.s:
digvibhāgastu tajjo'sti vadanānāṃ catuṣṭayāt /
pañcamasya yujitve tau parityaktanijātmakau // 211
15.d:
दिग्विभागस्तु तज्जोऽस्ति वदनानां चतुष्टयात् ।
